title.zh: 卷59 劉昶 蕭寶夤 蕭正表
title.en: Volume 59: Liu Chang, Xiao Baoyin, Xiao Zhengbiao
title.raw: 卷59 劉昶 蕭寶夤 蕭正表 Volume 59: Liu Chang, Xiao Baoyin, Xiao Zhengbiao

sentences.zh: 劉昶 蕭寶夤 蕭正表

translations.literal: Liu Chang, Xiao Baoyin, Xiao Zhengbiao
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang, Xiao Baoyin, and Xiao Zhengbiao

sentences.zh: 劉昶，字休道，義隆第九子也。

translations.literal: Liu Chang, courtesy name Xiudao, was the ninth son of Yilong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang, styled Xiudao, was the ninth son of Emperor Wen of Song (Yilong).

sentences.zh: 義隆時，封義陽王。

translations.literal: In Yilong's time he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: During Yilong's reign he was created Prince of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 兄駿以為征北將軍、徐州刺史、開府。

translations.literal: His elder brother Jun made him General Who Pacifies the North, Governor of Xuzhou, and Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Jun appointed him General Who Pacifies the North, regional inspector of Xuzhou, and commander of an independent staff.

sentences.zh: 及駿子子業立，昏狂肆暴，害其親屬，疑昶有異志。

translations.literal: When Jun's son Ziye came to the throne, he was muddled, wild, and wantonly violent, harmed his kin, and suspected Chang of divergent intentions.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun's son Ziye succeeded, that mad and brutal ruler slaughtered his own kin and came to suspect that Chang harbored other designs.

sentences.zh: 昶聞甚懼，遣典籤虞法生表求入朝，[1]以觀其意。

translations.literal: Chang heard and was greatly afraid; he sent his steward Yu Fasheng to memorialize requesting entry to court [1] in order to observe the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was terrified when he heard this and sent his chief clerk Yu Fasheng to request permission to come to court, hoping to gauge the emperor's intentions.

sentences.zh: 子業曰：「義陽與太宰謀反，我欲討之，今知求還，甚善。

translations.literal: Ziye said: "The Prince of Yiyang is plotting rebellion with the Grand Guardian; I mean to attack him. Now that I know he asks to return, that is very good.
translations.idiomatic: Ziye said, "The Prince of Yiyang is conspiring with the Grand Guardian to rebel. I was about to move against him, but now that he asks to return, so much the better.

sentences.zh: 」又屢詰法生：「義陽謀事，汝何故不啟？

translations.literal: " He also repeatedly interrogated Fasheng: "The Prince of Yiyang is plotting—why did you not report it?
translations.idiomatic: " He also pressed Fasheng again and again: "The Prince of Yiyang is plotting treason—why did you never tell me?"

sentences.zh: 」法生懼禍，走歸彭城。

translations.literal: " Fasheng feared calamity and fled back to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fasheng, fearing for his life, fled back to Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 昶欲襲建康，諸郡並不受命。

translations.literal: Chang wished to strike Jiankang, but none of the commanderies would obey his orders.
translations.idiomatic: Chang tried to march on Jiankang, but not a single commandery would follow his command.

sentences.zh: 和平六年，遂委母妻，攜妾吳氏作丈夫服，結義從六十餘人，間行來降。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Heping, he left behind his mother and wife, took his concubine Lady Wu dressed in men's attire, joined with more than sixty sworn followers, and came by secret paths to defect.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Heping (468), he abandoned his mother and wife, had his concubine Lady Wu dress as a man, gathered more than sixty sworn companions, and slipped away to surrender to the north.

sentences.zh: 在路多叛，隨昶至者二十許人。

translations.literal: Many deserted on the road; only about twenty followed Chang to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Many deserted along the way; only some twenty men reached the north with Chang.

sentences.zh: 昶雖學不淵洽，略覽子史，前後表啟，皆其自製。

translations.literal: Though Chang's learning was not profound, he had read somewhat in histories; all his memorials and reports before and after were composed by himself.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was not deeply learned, but he had browsed histories and composed all his own memorials and petitions.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉重之，尚武邑公主，拜侍中、征南將軍、駙馬都尉，封丹陽王。

translations.literal: The court honored him greatly, married him to Princess Wuyi of Shang, and appointed him Palace Attendant, General Who Conquers the South, Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Household, and Prince of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: The court held him in high esteem, gave him Princess Wuyi in marriage, and made him Palace Attendant, General Who Conquers the South, Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Household, and Prince of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 歲餘而公主薨，更尚建興長公主。

translations.literal: After little more than a year the princess died; he then married Princess Chang of Jianxing.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later the princess died, and he married Princess Chang of Jianxing.

sentences.zh: 昶好犬馬，愛武事，入國歷紀，猶布衣皂冠，同凶素之服。

translations.literal: Chang loved dogs and horses and delighted in military affairs; for the calendar since entering the state he still wore common cloth and black cap, the garb of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Chang loved horses and hounds and delighted in arms; for years after entering Wei he still wore plain cloth and a black cap, as if in mourning.

sentences.zh: 然呵詈童僕，音雜夷夏。

translations.literal: Yet he cursed and scolded page boys, his speech mixing barbarian and Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he abused his pages in a tongue that mixed barbarian speech with Chinese.

sentences.zh: 雖在公坐，諸王每侮弄之，或戾手齧臂，至於痛傷，笑呼之聲，聞于御聽。

translations.literal: Even when seated in formal assembly, the princes would constantly mock and bully him, sometimes twisting his hands and biting his arms until he was wounded in pain; their shouts of laughter reached the emperor's ears.
translations.idiomatic: Even at court the princes would mock and torment him—twisting his hands, biting his arms until he bled—and their laughter carried to the throne.

sentences.zh: 高祖每優假之，不以怪問。

translations.literal: Gaozu always treated him with extra favor and did not regard it as strange.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu always indulged him and never questioned the odd behavior.

sentences.zh: 至於陳奏本國事故，語及征役，則能斂容涕泗，悲動左右。

translations.literal: But when he memorialized on affairs of his native state, and his words touched on levies and service, he could compose his expression and weep; his grief moved those around him.
translations.idiomatic: When he spoke of his lost kingdom or of conscription and levies, he would compose himself and weep until all around him were moved.

sentences.zh: 而天性褊躁，喜怒不恒，每至威忿，楚朴特苦，引待南士，禮多不足，緣此人懷畏避。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was narrow and impatient, joy and anger unsteady; whenever wrath flared, beatings with the cudgel were especially harsh. He drew in and received southern gentlemen but his courtesy toward them was often insufficient; for this reason people bore fear and avoided him.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was touchy and quick-tempered; in fits of rage he beat servants cruelly with the rod. Though he gathered southern émigrés, he often slighted them, and many kept their distance out of fear.

sentences.zh: 太和初，轉內都坐大官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe he was transferred to Grand Supervisor of the Inner Palace Provisioners.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taihe era he was made Grand Supervisor of the Inner Palace Provisioners.

sentences.zh: 及蕭道成殺劉準，時遣諸將南伐，詔昶曰：「卿識機體運，先覺而來。

translations.literal: When Xiao Daocheng killed Liu Zhun, the court at that time sent generals south to campaign; the edict to Chang said: "You perceived the moment and the turn of fortune and came ahead of your time.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Daocheng murdered Liu Zhun, the court sent generals south on campaign. The edict to Chang read, "You read the times and came before it was too late.

sentences.zh: 卿宗廟不復血食，朕聞斯問，矜忿兼懷。

translations.literal: Your ancestral altars no longer receive blood sacrifices; when We heard this, pity and anger mingled in Our breast.
translations.idiomatic: Your ancestral temples stand empty of offerings. When We heard of it, pity and wrath filled Our heart alike.

sentences.zh: 今遣大將軍率南州甲卒，以伐逆竪，克蕩兇醜，翦除民害。

translations.literal: Now We send the Grand General with southern troops to punish the usurper, sweep away the vicious, and cut down harm to the people.
translations.idiomatic: We now send the Grand General at the head of southern armies to crush the rebel, sweep away the wicked, and rid the people of their scourge.

sentences.zh: 氛穢既清，即胙卿江南之土，以興蕃業。

translations.literal: Once the foul air is cleared, We shall invest you with the lands of Jiangnan to revive your feudal estate.
translations.idiomatic: When the land is pacified, We shall enfeoff you with the south and restore your house to its former glory.

sentences.zh: 」乃以本將軍與諸將同行。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was given his former rank as general and marched with the other generals.
translations.idiomatic: He was then confirmed in his former rank as general and marched with the other commanders.

sentences.zh: 路經徐州，哭拜其母舊堂，哀感從者。

translations.literal: Passing through Xuzhou, he wept and bowed at his mother's former hall, his grief moving those who accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: On the march through Xuzhou he wept and bowed at his mother's old hall until all who followed him were moved.

sentences.zh: 乃遍循故居，處處隕涕，左右亦莫不辛酸。

translations.literal: He then went everywhere through his old residences, weeping tears at each place; those around him also could not but taste bitterness.
translations.idiomatic: He walked through every old home, weeping at each turn, until even his attendants could not keep back their tears.

sentences.zh: 及至軍所，將欲臨陳，四面拜諸將士，自陳家國滅亡，蒙朝廷慈覆，辭理切至，聲氣激揚，涕泗橫流，三軍咸為感歎。

translations.literal: When he reached the army, about to draw up for battle, he bowed on all sides to the officers and men, himself declaring his state's ruin and the court's gracious shelter—his reasoning keen, voice fervent, tears streaming; the whole army was moved to sigh.
translations.idiomatic: When the army was about to engage, he bowed to the troops on every side, telling how his kingdom had fallen and how the court had sheltered him. His words were piercing, his voice fierce, tears streaming down his face, and the whole army sighed with him.

sentences.zh: 後昶恐雨水方降，表請還師，從之。

translations.literal: Later Chang feared the rainy season would set in and memorialized requesting withdrawal; his request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Later Chang, fearing the rains, asked to withdraw the army, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 又加儀同三司，領儀曹尚書。

translations.literal: He was further given the rank Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers and made Minister of the Armies of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was further given rank equal to the Three Ducal Ministers and appointed Minister of the Armies of Rites.

sentences.zh: 於時改革朝儀，詔昶與蔣少遊專主其事。

translations.literal: At that time court ritual was being reformed; Chang and Jiang Shaoyou were ordered to take charge of it exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: Court ritual was then being reformed, and Chang and Jiang Shaoyou were put solely in charge of the work.

sentences.zh: 昶條上舊式，略不遺忘。

translations.literal: Chang listed the old forms item by item, omitting almost nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Chang submitted the old forms point by point, forgetting scarcely a detail.

sentences.zh: 高祖引見於宣文堂，昶啟曰：「臣本國不造，私有虐政，不能廢昏立德，扶定傾危，萬里奔波，投蔭皇闕，仰賴天慈，以存首領。

translations.literal: Gaozu received him at the Xuanwen Hall; Chang opened: "My native state met misfortune and had a tyrannical regime; I could not depose the muddled and establish the enlightened, nor steady what was toppling. I ran ten thousand li and cast myself under the imperial shade, relying on Heaven's kindness to keep my head.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu received him in the Xuanculture Hall. Chang said, "My country was ruined by a tyrant. I could not remove the wicked and set the throne right, but fled a thousand leagues to seek shelter under your gate, trusting your mercy to spare my life.

sentences.zh: 然大耻未雪，痛愧纏心。

translations.literal: Yet great shame is unavenged; pain and shame twine about my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yet my great shame is still unavenged, and remorse gnaws at me.

sentences.zh: 屬逢陛下釐校之始，願垂曲恩，處臣邊戍，招集遺人，以雪私耻。

translations.literal: It happens that Your Majesty is at the beginning of ordering the realm; I beg a bending of favor, to place me on the frontier garrison, gather the scattered remnant, and wipe away private shame.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Your Majesty is putting the realm in order, I beg you to post me on the frontier, let me gather our scattered people, and redeem my private shame.

sentences.zh: 雖死之日，猶若生年。

translations.literal: Though the day I die, it will be as if I lived again.
translations.idiomatic: Even on the day I die, it will be as though I were born anew.

sentences.zh: 」悲泣良久。

translations.literal: " He wept in grief for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: He wept for a long time.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「卿投誠累紀，本邦湮滅，王者未能恤難矜災，良以為愧。

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "You have offered loyalty for years; your native state is extinguished. A king who could not pity disaster and commiserate calamity—We are truly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "You have served us faithfully for years while your homeland perished. That We could not sooner relieve your suffering is a source of shame to Us.

sentences.zh: 出蕃之日，請別當處分。

translations.literal: When the day comes to go out to your fief, request separate disposition.
translations.idiomatic: When the day comes for you to take up your post on the frontier, ask Us then for a separate assignment.

sentences.zh: 」後以昶女為鄉君。

translations.literal: " Later Chang's daughter was made Village Lady.
translations.idiomatic: Later his daughter was ennobled as Village Lady.

sentences.zh: 高祖臨宣文堂，見武興王楊集始。

translations.literal: Gaozu came to the Xuanwen Hall and received Yang Jishi, King of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu held audience in the Xuanwen Hall with Yang Jishi, King of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 既而引集始入宴，詔昶曰：「集始邊方之酋，不足以當諸侯之禮，但王者不遺小國之臣，況此蕃垂之主，故勞公卿於此。

translations.literal: Then he led Jishi in to the banquet and said to Chang: "Jishi is a chieftain of the borderlands, not sufficient for the rites due a feudal lord; yet a king does not disdain the ministers of small states—how much more this lord of a frontier realm—therefore We have troubled the high ministers here.
translations.idiomatic: He then brought Jishi in to feast and told Chang, "Jishi is a frontier chieftain, not truly fit for the rites of a feudal lord. Yet a king does not scorn the envoys of small states, still less a border king such as this, and so We have troubled you ministers to receive him.

sentences.zh: 」昶對曰：「陛下道化光被，自北而南，故巴漢之雄，遠覲天闕。

translations.literal: " Chang replied: "Your Majesty's transforming Way shines everywhere, from north to south; therefore the heroes of Ba and Han come from afar to behold the celestial gate.
translations.idiomatic: Chang replied, "Your transforming virtue shines from north to south, and so the chiefs of Ba and Han journey far to behold the imperial court.

sentences.zh: 臣猥瞻盛禮，實忻嘉遇。

translations.literal: Your servant has unworthily witnessed this grand ceremony and is truly glad at this excellent encounter.
translations.idiomatic: I am unworthy to witness such ceremony, yet I rejoice at this gracious occasion.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「武興、宕昌，於禮容並不閑備，向見集始，觀其舉動，有賢於彌承。

translations.literal: " Gaozu said: "Wuxing and Dangchang are both unskilled in ritual deportment. Just now, seeing Jishi and observing his bearing, he is more worthy than Micheng.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "The kings of Wuxing and Dangchang are both unversed in court ritual. Watching Jishi just now, I find him more capable than Micheng.

sentences.zh: 」昶對曰：「陛下惠洽普天，澤流無外，武興蕞爾，豈不食椹懷音。」

translations.literal: " Chang replied: "Your Majesty's kindness reaches all under Heaven, favor flowing without outer limit; how could tiny Wuxing fail to taste the mulberry and cherish the sound?"
translations.idiomatic: Chang replied, "Your grace fills the realm and flows beyond its borders. How could petty Wuxing fail to remember your kindness."

sentences.zh: 又為中書監。

translations.literal: He was also made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was also appointed Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 開建五等，封昶齊郡開國公，加宋王之號。

translations.literal: When the five ranks were established, Chang was enfeoffed as Duke of Qi commandery with a founding fief and given the title Prince of Song.
translations.idiomatic: When the five feudal ranks were instituted, Chang was created Duke of Qi with a founding fief and given the title Prince of Song.

sentences.zh: 十七年春，高祖臨經武殿，大議南伐，語及劉、蕭篡奪之事，昶每悲泣不已。

translations.literal: In spring of the seventeenth year Gaozu came to the Jingwu Hall for great deliberation on the southern campaign; when talk touched the Liu and Xiao usurpations, Chang wept in grief without cease.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the seventeenth year Gaozu held council in the Jingwu Hall on the southern expedition; whenever the Liu and Xiao usurpations were mentioned, Chang wept without end.

sentences.zh: 因奏曰：「臣本朝淪喪，艱毒備罹，冀恃國靈，釋臣私耻。

translations.literal: He then memorialized: "My native dynasty is lost, every hardship and poison I have suffered; I hope to rely on the state's numinous power to release my private shame.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "My dynasty is ruined and I have suffered every torment. I pray to lean on the state's might to wipe away my private shame.

sentences.zh: 」頓首拜謝。

translations.literal: " He knocked his head and bowed in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: He kowtowed in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 高祖亦為之流涕，禮之彌崇。

translations.literal: Gaozu also wept for it and honored him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu wept as well and treated him with still greater honor.

sentences.zh: 蕭賾雍州刺史曹虎之詐降也，詔昶以兵出義陽，無功而還。

translations.literal: When Xiao Ze's Governor of Yongzhou Cao Huzhi feigned surrender, Chang was ordered to lead troops out from Yiyang; he achieved nothing and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Huzhi, Governor of Yongzhou under Xiao Ze, pretended to surrender, Chang was sent against Yiyang but returned without success.

sentences.zh: 十八年，除使持節、都督吳越楚彭城諸軍事、大將軍，固辭，詔不許，又賜布千匹。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority and Commander-in-Chief of the armies of Wu, Yue, Chu, and Pengcheng; he firmly declined, the edict did not permit it, and he was further given a thousand bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was appointed Grand General with full credentials and command over the Wu, Yue, Chu, and Pengcheng theaters. He declined firmly, but the emperor would not hear of it and gave him a thousand bolts of cloth besides.

sentences.zh: 及發，高祖親餞之，命百僚賦詩贈昶，又以其文集一部賜昶。

translations.literal: When he set out, Gaozu personally saw him off with a farewell feast, ordered the hundred officials to compose poems to present to Chang, and also gave Chang a set of his own collected writings.
translations.idiomatic: When he marched, Gaozu himself gave him a farewell feast, ordered the court to compose parting poems, and presented him with a volume of his own writings.

sentences.zh: 高祖因以所製文筆示之，謂昶曰：「時契勝殘，事鍾文業，雖則不學，欲罷不能。

translations.literal: Gaozu thereupon showed him writings he had composed and said to Chang: "The age fits overcoming the cruel remnant; affairs turn on the enterprise of culture. Though I am unlearned, I wish to stop but cannot.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu showed him some pieces he had written and said, "The times call for ending violence and building culture. Though I am no scholar, I cannot lay down the brush.

sentences.zh: 脫思一見，故以相示。

translations.literal: If you care to look once, I therefore show them to you.
translations.idiomatic: If you care to read them, I offer them for your view.

sentences.zh: 雖無足味，聊復為笑耳。

translations.literal: Though they have no sufficient flavor, they may yet serve for a laugh.
translations.idiomatic: They are hardly worth reading, but may amuse you for a moment.

sentences.zh: 」其重昶如是。

translations.literal: " Such was the weight he gave Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he held Chang.

sentences.zh: 自昶之背彭城，至是久矣。

translations.literal: From the time Chang left Pengcheng until now was long.
translations.idiomatic: Long years had passed since Chang fled Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 其昔齋宇山池，並尚存立，昶更修繕，還處其中。

translations.literal: His former halls, pools, and mountain gardens still stood; Chang restored them and returned to dwell within.
translations.idiomatic: His old halls, gardens, and ponds still stood; Chang repaired them and moved back in.

sentences.zh: 不能綏邊懷物，撫接義故，而閨門喧猥，內外姦雜，前民舊吏，莫不慨歎焉。

translations.literal: He could not pacify the border and cherish men, nor comfort and receive old associates; instead the inner quarters were noisy and vulgar, inside and outside tangled in illicit relations—former subjects and old officials all sighed at it.
translations.idiomatic: He failed to win hearts on the frontier or treat old friends well; his household was disorderly and licentious within and without, and former subjects and retainers lamented it.

sentences.zh: 豫營墓於彭城西南，與三公主同塋而異穴。

translations.literal: He prepared a tomb southwest of Pengcheng, sharing a mound but separate chambers with the Third Princess.
translations.idiomatic: He prepared a tomb southwest of Pengcheng to share a mound but not a chamber with the Third Princess.

sentences.zh: 發石累之，墳崩，壓殺十餘人。

translations.literal: When stone was quarried and piled, the tomb mound collapsed and crushed more than ten men to death.
translations.idiomatic: While stone was being quarried and piled, the mound collapsed and killed more than ten workers.

sentences.zh: 後復移改，為公私費害。

translations.literal: Later it was moved and altered again, causing expense and harm to public and private.
translations.idiomatic: The site was moved again later, to the cost of public funds and private grief.

sentences.zh: 高祖南討，昶候駕於行宮，高祖遣侍中迎勞之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu campaigned south, Chang waited on the imperial carriage at the traveling palace; Gaozu sent a Palace Attendant to welcome and comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: On Gaozu's southern campaign Chang waited on him at the traveling palace, and Gaozu sent a Palace Attendant to greet and console him.

sentences.zh: 昶討蕭昭業司州，雖屢破賊軍，而義陽拒守不克，昶乃班師。

translations.literal: Chang campaigned against Xiao Zhaoye's Sizhou; though he repeatedly defeated rebel armies, Yiyang held out and could not be taken, and Chang withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: Chang attacked Sizhou under Xiao Zhaoye. Though he won several battles, Yiyang held firm and he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十九年，高祖在彭城，昶至入見。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Gaozu was at Pengcheng; Chang arrived and entered audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Gaozu was at Pengcheng; Chang came to audience.

sentences.zh: 昶曰：「臣奉敕專征，剋殄兇醜，徒勞士馬，久淹歲時，有損威靈，伏聽斧鉞。

translations.literal: Chang said: "Your servant received the edict for a dedicated campaign to destroy the vicious; I have only tired soldiers and horses, long delayed the seasons, and harmed imperial majesty—I bow to await the axe.
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "I was ordered on campaign to destroy the enemy, yet I have only wasted men and horses and dragged on for months, shaming your arms. I submit to your judgment.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「朕之此行，本無攻守之意，正欲伐罪弔民，宣威布德，二事既暢，不失本圖，朕亦無克而還，豈但卿也。」

translations.literal: " Gaozu said: "Our march this time had no intent of attack or defense from the start; We only wished to punish crime and comfort the people, spread majesty and spread virtue. Once these two matters were achieved, We did not miss Our original design. We too return without conquest—is it only you?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "This expedition was never meant for conquest alone. We came to punish the guilty, comfort the people, and spread virtue. Having done that, We are content to withdraw without victory—and not you alone."

sentences.zh: 十月，昶朝于京師。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Chang attended court at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Chang came to court at the capital.

sentences.zh: 高祖臨光極堂大選。

translations.literal: Gaozu came to the Guangji Hall for the great selection.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu held the great selection at the Guangji Hall.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「朝因月旦，欲評魏典。

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "The court, taking occasion of the first of the month, wishes to assess the Wei code.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "On this first of the month the court will review the Wei statutes.

sentences.zh: 夫典者，為國大綱，治民之柄。

translations.literal: Now a code is the great outline of a state, the handle for governing the people.
translations.idiomatic: A code is the great framework of a state and the instrument by which the people are governed.

sentences.zh: 君能好典則國治，不能則國亂。

translations.literal: If a ruler can cherish the code, the state is well governed; if not, the state falls into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: If a ruler honors the code, the realm is well ordered; if not, it falls into chaos.

sentences.zh: 我國家昔在恒代，隨時制作，非通世之長典。

translations.literal: Our state formerly at Hengdai made institutions according to the times; they were not a lasting code for all ages.
translations.idiomatic: When our state was still at Hengdai we made laws for the moment, not a code meant to last for all time.

sentences.zh: 故自夏及秋，親議條制。

translations.literal: Therefore from summer through autumn We personally deliberated articles and regulations.
translations.idiomatic: From summer through autumn I have personally debated every article.

sentences.zh: 或言唯能是寄，不必拘門，朕以為不爾。

translations.literal: Some say that only talent should be entrusted and one need not be bound by lineage; We do not think so.
translations.idiomatic: Some say office should go only to talent and not be bound by family rank. I do not agree.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 當今之世，仰祖質朴，清濁同流，混齊一等，君子小人名品無別，此殊為不可。

translations.literal: In the present age, looking up to the ancestors' plain simplicity, pure and turbid flow in one stream, mixed and leveled in one rank—gentleman and petty man without distinction in name and grade; this is especially impossible.
translations.idiomatic: In our day, when men invoke the plain ways of old, noble and base are mingled in one stream and gentleman and commoner stand undistinguished. That cannot stand.

sentences.zh: 我今八族以上，士人品第有九，九品之外，小人之官，復有七等。

translations.literal: We now have for the eight clans and above nine grades of gentry rank; beyond the nine grades, offices for petty men have seven further grades.
translations.idiomatic: For the eight great clans and above I have set nine grades of gentry rank; below the ninth grade, offices for commoners have seven further ranks.

sentences.zh: 若苟有其人，可起家為三公。

translations.literal: If there is truly such a man, he may rise from obscurity to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: If the man truly exists, he may rise from nothing to one of the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 正恐賢才難得，不可止為一人，渾我典制。

translations.literal: We only fear that worthy talent is hard to obtain and one cannot for a single man blur Our code and institutions.
translations.idiomatic: I fear only that worthy men are rare and that the code must not be bent for one man's sake alone.

sentences.zh: 故令班鏡九流，清一朝軌，使千載之後，我得髣像唐虞，卿等依俙元、凱。

translations.literal: Therefore We order the ranks to mirror the nine streams, clarify the court's measure, so that a thousand years hence We may resemble Tang and Yu, and you may take Yuan and Kai as models.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I set ranks to mirror the nine currents and clarify the court's standards, so that a thousand years hence we may resemble the age of Yao and Shun, and you may take Yuan and Kai as your models.

sentences.zh: 」昶對曰：「陛下光宅中區，惟新朝典，刊正九流，為不朽之法，豈唯髣像唐虞，固以有高三代。

translations.literal: " Chang replied: "Your Majesty illuminates the central realm and renews the court code, correcting the nine streams into an immortal law—not only resembling Tang and Yu, but indeed surpassing the Three Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Chang replied, "Your Majesty has brought order to the realm and renewed our institutions, fixing the nine ranks into law that will not perish. You do not merely resemble Yao and Shun—you surpass the Three Dynasties."

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「國家本來有一事可慨。

translations.literal: " Gaozu said: "The state from the beginning has had one matter worth lament.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "There is one thing about this state that has always grieved me."

sentences.zh: 可慨者何？

translations.literal: What is worth lament?
translations.idiomatic: What is it?

sentences.zh: 恒無公言得失。

translations.literal: Constantly there was no open speech on right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: There has never been frank discussion of what is right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 今卿等各盡其心。

translations.literal: Now each of you should exhaust your hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Today I ask each of you to speak your mind fully.

sentences.zh: 人君患不能納羣下之諫，為臣患不能盡忠於主。

translations.literal: A ruler's worry is inability to accept remonstrance from below; a minister's worry is inability to exhaust loyalty to his lord.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler's fault is failing to heed counsel; a minister's fault is failing to speak honestly to his lord.

sentences.zh: 朕今舉一人，如有不可，卿等盡言其失；

translations.literal: We now nominate one man; if there is anything unsuitable, each of you speak fully of his faults;
translations.idiomatic: I will now propose one man for office. If he is unfit, speak freely of his faults;

sentences.zh: 若有才能而朕所不識者，宜各舉所知。

translations.literal: if there is talent We do not know, each should nominate whom you know.
translations.idiomatic: and if you know able men I have not heard of, each should name whom you know.

sentences.zh: 朕當虛己延納。

translations.literal: We shall empty Ourselves and extend reception.
translations.idiomatic: I will receive your words with an open mind.

sentences.zh: 若能如此，能舉則受賞，不言則有罪。」

translations.literal: If you can do thus, those who nominate receive reward; those who do not speak incur guilt."
translations.idiomatic: If you do so, those who speak up will be rewarded; those who stay silent will be punished."

sentences.zh: 昶適子承緒，主所生也。

translations.literal: Chang's eldest son by the principal wife was Chengxu, born to the mistress.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's heir Chengxu was born to his concubine rather than his principal wife.

sentences.zh: 少而尫疾。

translations.literal: From youth he was frail and sickly.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was frail and sickly.

sentences.zh: 尚高祖妹彭城長公主，為駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: He married Gaozu's younger sister Princess Chang of Pengcheng and was made Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He married Gaozu's sister, Princess Chang of Pengcheng, and was made Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Household.

sentences.zh: 先昶卒，贈員外常侍。

translations.literal: He died before Chang; posthumously he was given the title Regular Attendant Outside the Number.
translations.idiomatic: He died before Chang and was posthumously given the title Regular Attendant Outside the Number.

sentences.zh: 長子文遠，次輝，字重昌，並皆疏狂，昶深慮不能守其爵封。

translations.literal: The eldest son was Wenyuan; the second was Hui, styled Chongchang. Both were dissolute and wild, and Chang deeply feared they could not preserve their titles and fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son was Wenyuan and his second Hui, courtesy name Chongchang. Both were reckless and unrestrained, and Liu Chang worried they would be unable to hold their rank and fief.

sentences.zh: 然輝猶小，未多罪過，乃以為世子，襲封。

translations.literal: Yet Hui was still young and had not many offenses, so he was made heir and inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was still young, however, and had not yet committed many wrongs, so he was made heir and inherited the fief.

sentences.zh: 正始初，尚蘭陵長公主，世宗第二姊也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengshi he married the Princess of Lanling, the second elder sister of Emperor Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengshi era he married the Princess of Lanling, Emperor Xuanwu's second elder sister.

sentences.zh: 拜員外常侍。

translations.literal: He was granted the post of Regular Attendant Outside the Body.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Regular Attendant Outside the Body.

sentences.zh: 公主頗嚴妬，輝嘗私幸主侍婢有身，主笞殺之。

translations.literal: The princess was quite strict and jealous; Hui once secretly favored the princess's waiting maid, who became pregnant; the princess flogged her to death.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was fiercely jealous. When Hui secretly slept with her waiting maid and the maid became pregnant, the princess beat her to death.

sentences.zh: 剖其孕子，節解，以草裝實婢腹，裸以示輝。

translations.literal: She cut open the pregnancy, dismembered it limb by limb, stuffed the maid's belly with straw, and displayed her naked to Hui.
translations.idiomatic: She cut out the unborn child, dismembered it, stuffed straw into the maid's belly, and displayed the naked corpse to Hui.

sentences.zh: 輝遂忿憾，疏薄公主。

translations.literal: Hui then nursed resentful grievance and grew cold and distant toward the princess.
translations.idiomatic: Hui nursed bitter resentment and grew cold toward his wife.

sentences.zh: 公主姊因入聽講，言其故於靈太后，太后敕清河王懌窮其事。

translations.literal: The princess's elder sister, entering to hear lectures, told the cause to Empress Dowager Ling; the empress dowager ordered Prince of Qinghe Yi to investigate the affair thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Her elder sister, attending lectures at court, told Empress Dowager Ling what had happened. The empress dowager ordered Prince Yi of Qinghe to investigate to the bottom.

sentences.zh: 懌與高陽王雍、廣平王懷奏其不和之狀，無可為夫婦之理，請離婚，削除封位。

translations.literal: Yi with Prince Yong of Gaoyang and Prince Huai of Guangping memorialized their disharmony, that there was no reason they could remain husband and wife, and asked divorce and removal of enfeoffment and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, Prince Yong of Gaoyang, and Prince Huai of Guangping reported their bitter strife, arguing that they could no longer live as husband and wife, and asked for divorce and the stripping of Hui's titles.

sentences.zh: 太后從之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager agreed.

sentences.zh: 公主在宮周歲，高陽王及劉騰等皆為言於太后。

translations.literal: The princess was in the palace a full year; Prince Yong of Gaoyang and Liu Teng and others all spoke on her behalf to the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: After the princess had spent a year in the palace, Prince Yong of Gaoyang, Liu Teng, and others all pleaded her case to the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 太后慮其不改，未許之，雍等屢請不已，聽復舊義。

translations.literal: The empress dowager feared they would not change and did not permit it; Yong and the others repeatedly asked without cease, and she allowed restoration of the old bond.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager feared they would not reform and at first refused. Yong and the others persisted, however, until she allowed the marriage to be restored.

sentences.zh: 太后流涕送公主，誡令謹護。

translations.literal: The empress dowager wept as she sent the princess off and admonished her to be cautious and restrained.
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, the empress dowager sent the princess back and warned her to be careful and restrained.

sentences.zh: 正光初，輝又私淫張陳二氏女。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengguang, Hui again secretly debauched the daughters of the Zhang and Chen families.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengguang era, Hui again secretly slept with daughters of the Zhang and Chen families.

sentences.zh: 公主更不檢惡，主姑陳留公主共相扇奬，遂與輝復致忿爭。

translations.literal: The princess no longer checked or forbade wickedness; her aunt the Princess of Chenliu together fanned and encouraged them, and thus with Hui again came to angry quarrel.
translations.idiomatic: The princess no longer tried to restrain him. Her aunt, the Princess of Chenliu, encouraged the affair, and she and Hui quarreled again in anger.

sentences.zh: 輝推主墮床，手脚毆蹈，主遂傷胎，輝懼罪逃逸。

translations.literal: Hui pushed the mistress from the bed and beat and trampled her hands and feet; the mistress thus miscarried; Hui, fearing punishment, fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hui threw the princess from the bed and trampled her hands and feet. She miscarried, and fearing punishment Hui fled.

sentences.zh: 靈太后召清河王懌決其事，二家女髠笞付宮，兄弟皆坐鞭刑，徙配敦煌為兵。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling summoned Prince of Qinghe Yi to decide the affair; the two families' daughters were shaved and flogged and handed over at the palace; the brothers were all punished with the whip and banished assigned to Dunhuang as soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling summoned Prince Yi of Qinghe to judge the matter. The Zhang and Chen daughters were shaved and flogged at court; their brothers were whipped and exiled to Dunhuang as soldiers.

sentences.zh: 公主因傷致薨，太后親臨慟哭，舉哀太極東堂，出葬城西，太后親送數里，盡哀而還。

translations.literal: The princess died from her wounds; the empress dowager came in person to mourn and weep; mourning was raised at the eastern hall of the Supreme Ultimate; burial was outside the western wall; the empress dowager personally escorted several li and returned only when grief was spent.
translations.idiomatic: The princess died of her injuries. The empress dowager came in person to mourn and weep, and mourning was held at the eastern hall of the Supreme Ultimate. She was buried outside the western wall; the empress dowager escorted the procession for several li and returned only when her grief was exhausted.

sentences.zh: 謂侍中崔光曰：「向哭所以過哀者，追念公主為輝頓辱非一，乃不關言，能為隱忍，古今寧有此！

translations.literal: She said to Palace Attendant Cui Guang: "The reason my weeping just now was excessively mournful is that recalling how the princess suffered repeated humiliation from Hui, yet said nothing about it and could endure in silence—was there ever such a thing in antiquity or today!
translations.idiomatic: She said to Palace Attendant Cui Guang, "I wept so bitterly just now because I recalled how the princess suffered repeated insults from Hui yet never complained and endured in silence. When was there ever such a thing in all history!

sentences.zh: 此所以痛之。

translations.literal: This is why I grieve for her.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I grieve for her so.

sentences.zh: 」後執輝於河內之溫縣，幽于司州，將加死刑，會赦得免。

translations.literal: " Later Hui was seized at Wen in Henei, imprisoned in Si Province, and was to receive the death penalty; an amnesty came and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: " Later Hui was captured at Wen in Henei and held in Si Province, where he was sentenced to death; an amnesty spared him.

sentences.zh: 三年，復其官爵，遷征虜將軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: In the third year his office and title were restored; he was moved to General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later his rank and title were restored, and he was made General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 四年，輝卒，家遂衰頓，無復可紀。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Hui died; the house then declined and collapsed, with nothing further worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Hui died, and the family fell into decline, with nothing further worth recording.

sentences.zh: 文遠，歷步兵校尉、前將軍。

translations.literal: Wenyuan successively held the posts of Commandant of Footsoldiers and General of the Vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyuan served as Commandant of Footsoldiers and then General of the Vanguard.

sentences.zh: 景明初，為統軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingming he was made an area commander.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingming era he was made an area commander.

sentences.zh: 在壽春，坐謀殺刺史王肅以壽春叛，事發伏法。

translations.literal: At Shouyang he was judged for plotting to kill Inspector Wang Su so as to rebel with Shouyang; when the affair was exposed he was executed by law.
translations.idiomatic: While at Shouyang he plotted to murder Inspector Wang Su and rebel with the city. When the plot was discovered he was executed.

sentences.zh: 有通直郎劉武英者，太和十九年從淮南內附，自云劉裕弟長沙景王道憐之曾孫，賜爵建寧子，司徒外兵參軍，稍轉步兵校尉、游擊將軍，卒于河內太守。

translations.literal: There was a Direct Attendant-in-Ordinary Liu Wuying who in the nineteenth year of Taihe came from Huainan to submit inward, declaring himself a great-grandson of Liu Daoling, Prince Jing of Changsha, younger brother of Liu Yu; he was granted the title Baron of Jianning, was an Outer Troops Aide of the Minister of Education, and was gradually transferred to Commandant of Footsoldiers and General Who Rogues, dying as Administrator of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: A Direct Attendant-in-Ordinary named Liu Wuying came north from Huainan in Taihe year 19, claiming to be a great-grandson of Prince Jing of Changsha, Liu Yu's younger brother. He was enfeoffed as Baron of Jianning, served as Outer Troops Aide under the Minister of Education, rose to Commandant of Footsoldiers and General Who Rogues, and died while serving as Administrator of Henei.

sentences.zh: 而昶不以為族親也。

translations.literal: Yet Chang did not regard him as a kinsman of the clan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang did not acknowledge him as a relative.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶夤，字智亮，蕭鸞第六子，寶卷母弟也。

translations.literal: Xiao Baoyin, styled Zhiliang, was the sixth son of Xiao Luan, younger brother of the mother of Emperor Baojuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Baoyin, courtesy name Zhiliang, was the sixth son of Xiao Luan and the younger brother of Emperor Baojuan's mother.

sentences.zh: 鸞之竊位，封寶夤建安王。

translations.literal: When Luan usurped the throne, he enfeoffed Baoyin as Prince of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Luan seized the throne he enfeoffed Baoyin as Prince of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 寶卷立，以為車騎將軍、開府，領石頭戍軍事。

translations.literal: When Baojuan took the throne, he was made General of Chariots and Cavalry, with an opening office, and put in charge of the military affairs of the Shitou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When Baojuan acceded he was made General of Chariots and Cavalry with an opening office and put in charge of the Shitou garrison.

sentences.zh: 寶卷昏狂，其直後劉靈運等謀奉寶夤，密遣報寶夤，寶夤許之。

translations.literal: Baojuan was benighted and mad; his palace guard attendant Liu Lingyun and others plotted to install Baoyin; they secretly sent word to Baoyin, and Baoyin agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Baojuan was deranged. His personal guard Liu Lingyun and others plotted to put Baoyin on the throne and secretly sent word to him; Baoyin agreed.

sentences.zh: 遂迎寶夤率石頭文武向其臺城，稱警蹕，百姓隨從者數百人。

translations.literal: They then welcomed Baoyin, leading the civil and military officials of Shitou toward the imperial city, proclaiming the imperial progress; several hundred common people followed.
translations.idiomatic: They then brought Baoyin out, leading Shitou's civil and military officials toward the palace and proclaiming an imperial progress, with several hundred civilians following.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，城門閉，乃燒三尚及建業城，城上射殺數人，眾乃奔散。

translations.literal: It happened to be dusk; the city gates were closed; they then burned the Three Shang offices and Jiankang city; those on the wall shot and killed several men, and the crowd then fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: By dusk the gates were closed. They burned the Three Shang offices and Jiankang's outer wall; defenders on the wall shot several people dead, and the crowd scattered.

sentences.zh: 寶夤棄車步走，部尉執送之，自列為人所逼，寶卷亦不罪責也。

translations.literal: Baoyin abandoned his carriage and fled on foot; a district captain seized and sent him back; he himself listed that he had been forced by others, and Baojuan also did not punish or blame him.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin abandoned his carriage and fled on foot. A district captain caught and returned him. He claimed he had been coerced, and Baojuan did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 寶卷弟寶融僭立，以寶夤為衞將軍、南徐州刺史，改封鄱陽王。

translations.literal: Baojuan's younger brother Baorong usurped the throne; he made Baoyin General of the Guard and Inspector of Southern Xuzhou, changing his enfeoffment to Prince of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Baojuan's younger brother Baorong seized the throne, he made Baoyin General of the Guard and Inspector of Southern Xuzhou and changed his title to Prince of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍既克建業，殺其兄弟，將害寶夤，以兵守之，未至嚴急。

translations.literal: After Xiao Yan had taken Jiankang and killed their brothers, he was about to harm Baoyin; he placed troops to guard him, but the guard was not yet strict or urgent.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiao Yan captured Jiankang and killed the Xiao princes, he planned to kill Baoyin too and placed guards around him, though the confinement was not yet severe.

sentences.zh: 其家閹人顏文智與左右麻拱、黃神密計，穿牆夜出寶夤。

translations.literal: His household eunuch Yan Wenzhi with attendants Ma Gong and Huang Shen secretly plotted, broke through the wall by night, and brought Baoyin out.
translations.idiomatic: His household eunuch Yan Wenzhi, together with attendants Ma Gong and Huang Shen, plotted secretly, broke through a wall at night, and brought Baoyin out.

sentences.zh: 具小船於江岸，脫本衣服，著烏布襦，腰繫千許錢，潛赴江畔，躡屩徒步，脚無全皮。

translations.literal: They prepared a small boat on the riverbank; they stripped his formal dress and put on a black cloth jacket; at the waist he tied more than a thousand cash; they stole to the riverbank; treading sandals he went on foot; his feet had no whole skin.
translations.idiomatic: They had a small boat waiting on the bank. They stripped his court robes and dressed him in a black cloth jacket, tied a thousand-odd cash at his waist, and stole to the river. He walked in sandals until no skin on his feet remained whole.

sentences.zh: 防守者至明追之，寶夤假為釣者，隨流上下十餘里，追者不疑，待散，乃度西岸。

translations.literal: The guards pursued at dawn; Baoyin pretended to be a fisherman, drifting up and down the stream more than ten li; the pursuers did not suspect; when they dispersed, he then crossed to the west bank.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the guards gave chase. Baoyin played the fisherman, drifting up and down the river for more than ten li until the pursuers passed him by, then crossed to the west bank.

sentences.zh: 遂委命投華文榮。

translations.literal: He then entrusted his life and threw himself on Hua Wenrong.
translations.idiomatic: He then entrusted his life to Hua Wenrong.

sentences.zh: 文榮與其從子天龍、惠連等三人，棄家將寶夤遁匿山澗，賃驢乘之，晝伏宵行，景明二年至壽春之東城戍。

translations.literal: Wenrong with his followers Tianlong, Huilian, and three others abandoned their families, taking Baoyin to hide in mountain ravines, hired donkeys to ride, lay by day and marched by night, and in the second year of Jingming reached the eastern-wall garrison of Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wenrong, with his nephews Tianlong and Huilian and three others, abandoned their families and hid Baoyin in mountain ravines. They rode hired donkeys, marched by night and lay hidden by day, and in Jingming year 2 reached Shouyang's eastern garrison.

sentences.zh: 戍主杜元倫推檢，知實蕭氏子也，以禮延待，馳告揚州刺史、任城王澄，澄以車馬侍衞迎之。

translations.literal: Garrison chief Du Yuanlun examined and investigated, knew he was truly a son of the Xiao house, received him with ritual courtesy, sent word in haste to Yang Province Inspector, Prince of Rencheng Cheng, and Cheng came with carriage, horses, and guards to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison chief Du Yuanlun investigated and confirmed he was a true son of the Xiao house. He received him with ceremony and sent urgent word to Yang Province Inspector Prince Cheng of Rencheng, who came with carriage, horses, and escort to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 時年十六，徒步憔悴，見者以為掠賣生口也。

translations.literal: He was then sixteen; on foot, haggard and worn, viewers thought him a kidnapped captive being sold.
translations.idiomatic: He was sixteen, on foot and haggard; onlookers took him for a kidnapped slave being sold.

sentences.zh: 澄待以客禮。

translations.literal: Cheng received him with guest rites.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng treated him as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 乃請喪居斬衰之服，[3]澄遣人曉示情禮，以喪兄之制，給其齊衰，寶夤從命。

translations.literal: He then asked for the hemp mourning of a murdered lord in the highest degree of bereavement; [3] Cheng sent men to explain the proper feeling and ritual, and in the rites for a murdered elder brother gave him the hemp of the next degree; Baoyin obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to wear the deepest mourning for a slain sovereign. Cheng sent men to explain proper ritual and gave him the second-degree hemp mourning prescribed for a slain elder brother; Baoyin obeyed.

sentences.zh: 澄率官僚赴弔，寶夤居處有禮，不飲酒食肉，輟笑簡言，一同極哀之節。

translations.literal: Cheng led the officials to offer condolence; Baoyin's dwelling and conduct had ritual propriety; he did not drink wine or eat meat; he ceased laughter and spoke briefly, all one with the utmost of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng led the officials to mourn. Baoyin conducted himself with full propriety: no wine or meat, no laughter, speech kept brief — all in the deepest mourning.

sentences.zh: 壽春多其故義，皆受慰唁，唯不見夏侯一族，以夏侯同蕭衍故也。

translations.literal: In Shouyang many of his old associates came; all received his comfort and condolence; only he did not see the Xiahou clan, because the Xiahous were associated with Xiao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Many of his old associates in Shouyang came to offer condolences, and he received them all — except the Xiahou clan, who were connected to Xiao Yan.

sentences.zh: 改日造澄，澄深器重之。

translations.literal: On another day he visited Cheng; Cheng deeply valued him.
translations.idiomatic: On another day he called on Cheng, who came to prize him deeply.

sentences.zh: 景明三年閏四月，詔曰：「蕭寶夤深識機運，歸誠有道，冒險履屯，投命絳闕，微子、陳韓亦曷以過也。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingming, intercalary fourth month, an edict said: "Xiao Baoyin deeply perceives the turns of fortune, returned in sincerity to the Way, braved danger and tread hardship, cast his life on the scarlet gate — not even Weizi and Chen Han could surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fourth month of Jingming year 3 an edict said, "Xiao Baoyin has read the times aright, returned in loyalty to the righteous path, braved danger through hardship, and offered his life at the imperial gate — not even Weizi or Chen Han could have done more.

sentences.zh: [4]可遣羽林監、領主書劉桃符詣彼迎接。

translations.literal: [4] One may dispatch the Feathered Forest Supervisor and Chief of Palace Scribes Liu Taofu to go there to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatch Feathered Forest Supervisor and Chief of Palace Scribes Liu Taofu to go and escort him here.

sentences.zh: 其資生所須之物，及衣冠、車馬、在京邸館，付尚書悉令豫備。

translations.literal: The things required for his livelihood, as well as robes and caps, carriage and horses, and lodging at the capital — charge the Masters of Writing to prepare them all in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Let the Masters of Writing prepare in advance everything he will need for daily life, as well as robes, carriage, horses, and quarters in the capital.

sentences.zh: 」及至京師，世宗禮之甚重。

translations.literal: " When he reached the capital, Emperor Xuanwu honored him heavily.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the capital, Emperor Xuanwu received him with great honor.

sentences.zh: 伏訴闕下，請兵南伐，雖遇暴風大雨，終不暫移。

translations.literal: He prostrated and appealed below the palace gate, begging troops for a southern campaign; though violent wind and heavy rain came, he never moved for a moment.
translations.idiomatic: He prostrated himself at the palace gate, begging for troops to campaign south, and though storms struck he never stirred.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，蕭衍江州刺史陳伯之與其長史褚冑等自壽春歸降，[5]請軍立效。

translations.literal: That winter Liang's Inspector of Jiangzhou Chen Bozhi with his chief clerk Chu Zhou and others returned from Shouyang to surrender; [5] they asked for an army to establish merit.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Liang's Jiangzhou Inspector Chen Bozhi and his chief clerk Chu Zhou surrendered from Shouyang, asking to lead troops for the Wei cause.

sentences.zh: 世宗以寶夤誠懇及伯之所陳，時不可失，四年二月，乃引八座門下入議部分之方。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu, because Baoyin was earnest and sincere and because of what Bozhi reported, that the time could not be lost, in the second month of the fourth year summoned the Eight Dignitaries and Gate Ministers to discuss plans for division and deployment.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu judged that Baoyin's earnestness and Chen Bozhi's offer made delay impossible. In the second month of year 4 he summoned the Eight Dignitaries and palace ministers to plan the campaign.

sentences.zh: 四月，除使持節、都督東揚南徐兗三州諸軍事、鎮東將軍、東揚州刺史、[6]丹陽郡開國公、齊王，配兵一萬，令且據東城，待秋冬大舉。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he was made Commissioner with credentials, Area Commander of the military affairs of the three provinces Eastern Yang, Southern Xu, and Yan, General Who Pacifies the East, Inspector of Eastern Yang, [6] Duke of Danyang Commandery and founding noble, Prince of Qi, with ten thousand troops assigned, ordered to hold the eastern wall for the time being and await the great stroke in autumn and winter.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he was appointed Commissioner with credentials, commander of the armies of Eastern Yang, Southern Xu, and Yan, General Who Pacifies the East, Inspector of Eastern Yang, Duke of Danyang and Prince of Qi, with ten thousand troops. He was ordered to hold the eastern wall until the major autumn campaign.

sentences.zh: 寶夤明當拜命，其夜慟哭。

translations.literal: Baoyin was to receive the appointment the next day; that night he wept in anguish.
translations.idiomatic: The night before he was to receive his appointment, Baoyin wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 至晨，備禮策授，賜車馬什物，給虎賁五百人，事從豐厚，猶不及劉昶之優隆也。

translations.literal: At dawn the full ritual of investiture by patent was prepared; carriage, horses, and objects were granted; five hundred tiger guards were supplied; the affair followed rich and thick treatment, yet still fell short of Liu Chang's exceptional favor.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he received full investiture with rich gifts, five hundred tiger guards, and every mark of favor — yet still less than the extraordinary honors shown Liu Chang.

sentences.zh: 又任其募天下壯勇，得數千人。

translations.literal: He was also allowed to recruit valiant men throughout the realm and got several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He was also allowed to recruit brave men throughout the realm and gathered several thousand.

sentences.zh: 以文智三人等為積弩將軍，文榮等三人為強弩將軍，並為軍主。

translations.literal: Wenzhi and the other three were made generals of powerful crossbows; Wenrong and the other three were made generals of strong crossbows, all as army commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Wenzhi and three others were made generals of powerful crossbows; Hua Wenrong and three others generals of strong crossbows — all as army commanders.

sentences.zh: 寶夤雖少羇流，而志性雅重，過期猶絕酒肉，慘形悴色，蔬食粗衣，未嘗嬉笑。

translations.literal: Though Baoyin was young and long a hostage in exile, his will and nature were elegant and weighty; past the mourning term he still abstained from wine and meat; his form was haggard and his color wasted; he ate vegetables and wore coarse cloth and never laughed or smiled.
translations.idiomatic: Though young and long in exile, Baoyin was grave and refined by nature. Past the mourning period he still abstained from wine and meat, ate plain food, wore coarse clothes, and never laughed.

sentences.zh: 及被命當南伐，貴要多相憑託，門庭賓客若市，書記相尋，寶夤接對報復，不失其理。

translations.literal: When he was ordered to campaign south, the great and powerful relied on him in multitudes; his gate and courtyard had guests like a market; letters and records followed one after another, and Baoyin received and answered without losing reason.
translations.idiomatic: When ordered south, the powerful crowded his gate like a market. Letters piled up, yet he answered each without losing propriety.

sentences.zh: 正始元年三月，寶夤行達汝陰，東城已陷，遂停壽春之栖賢寺。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Zhengshi, Baoyin on his march reached Ruyin; the eastern wall had already fallen, so he stopped at the Qixian Temple in Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Zhengshi year 1 Baoyin reached Ruyin. The eastern wall had already fallen, so he halted at the Qixian Temple in Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 值賊將姜慶真內侵，士民響附，圍逼壽春，遂據外郭。

translations.literal: It happened that the rebel general Jiang Qingzhen invaded within; officers and people responded and attached themselves; he besieged and pressed Shouyang and thus seized the outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel general Jiang Qingzhen invaded from within. Local officers and people rallied to him, besieged Shouyang, and seized the outer city.

sentences.zh: 寶夤躬貫甲冑，率下擊之，自四更交戰，至明日申時，賊旅彌盛。

translations.literal: Baoyin personally donned armor and helmet, led his men to strike them, and from the fourth watch they fought until the third hour of the next day; the rebel troops grew ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin donned armor himself and led his men into battle from the fourth watch until midafternoon the next day, but the rebel force only grew stronger.

sentences.zh: 寶夤以眾寡無援，退入金城。

translations.literal: Baoyin, because his force was few and had no relief, withdrew into the inner citadel.
translations.idiomatic: Outnumbered and without relief, Baoyin withdrew into the inner citadel.

sentences.zh: 又出相國東門，率眾力戰，始破走之。

translations.literal: He again went out through the eastern gate of the Xiangguo district, led the multitude in fierce battle, and at last routed and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: He sallied out through the eastern gate of the Xiangguo quarter, fought hard, and at last routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 當寶夤壽春之戰，勇冠諸軍，聞見者莫不壯之。

translations.literal: At Baoyin's battle at Shouyang, his courage topped all the armies; those who heard and saw were all stirred.
translations.idiomatic: In the battle at Shouyang, Baoyin's courage topped every army; all who witnessed it were stirred.

sentences.zh: 七月，還京師，改封梁郡開國公，食邑八百戶。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he returned to the capital, was changed to Duke of Liang Commandery and founding noble, with a fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he returned to the capital and was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Liang Commandery with a fief of eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 及中山王英南伐，寶夤又表求征。

translations.literal: When Prince Ying of Zhongshan campaigned south, Baoyin again memorialized asking to campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Ying of Zhongshan marched south, Baoyin again petitioned to join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 乃為使持節、鎮東將軍、別將以繼英，配羽林、虎賁五百人。

translations.literal: He was then made Commissioner with credentials, General Who Pacifies the East, and a separate commander to follow after Ying, with five hundred Feathered Forest and tiger guards assigned.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Commissioner with credentials, General Who Pacifies the East, and detached commander under Ying, with five hundred Feathered Forest and tiger guards.

sentences.zh: 與英頻破衍軍，乘勝遂攻鍾離。

translations.literal: With Ying he repeatedly defeated Liang armies and, riding victory, then attacked Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: With Ying he repeatedly defeated Liang forces and pressed the attack on Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 淮水汎溢，寶夤與英狼狽引退，士卒死沒者十四五。

translations.literal: The Huai River overflowed its banks; Baoyin and Ying withdrew in disorder; soldiers who drowned and perished were four or five in ten.
translations.idiomatic: The Huai flooded. Baoyin and Ying retreated in disorder; four or five soldiers in ten drowned or died.

sentences.zh: 有司奏寶夤守東橋不固，軍敗由之，處以極法。

translations.literal: The offices memorialized that Baoyin had defended the eastern bridge poorly and that the army's defeat arose from this, and that he should receive the extreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: The offices reported that Baoyin had failed to hold the eastern bridge, causing the defeat, and recommended the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「寶夤因難投誠，宜加矜貸，可恕死，免官削爵還第。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "Baoyin, in difficulty, threw himself on our sincerity; he should receive added compassion and pardon; death may be forgiven; dismiss him from office, strip his title, and return him to his house."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Baoyin came to us in adversity; he deserves mercy. Spare his life, strip his office and title, and send him home."

sentences.zh: 尋尚南陽長公主，賜帛一千匹，并給禮具。

translations.literal: Soon he married the Princess of Nanyang; one thousand bolts of silk were granted, and wedding implements were also supplied.
translations.idiomatic: He soon married the Princess of Nanyang. He was granted a thousand bolts of silk and full wedding provisions.

sentences.zh: 公主有婦德，事寶夤盡肅雍之禮，雖好合積年，而敬事不替。

translations.literal: The princess had wifely virtue; in serving Baoyin she fully observed respectful and harmonious rites; though fond of each other for accumulated years, her reverent service did not slacken.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was virtuous as a wife and observed every mark of respectful harmony toward Baoyin. Though they had been married for years, her dutiful devotion never slackened.

sentences.zh: 寶夤每入室，公主必立以待之，相遇如賓，自非太妃疾篤，未曾歸休。

translations.literal: Whenever Baoyin entered the chamber the princess always stood to await him; they met like guests; unless the queen mother's illness was grave, he never retired to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Baoyin entered her room the princess stood to greet him; they treated each other like guests. Unless the queen dowager was gravely ill, he never retired early.

sentences.zh: 寶夤器性溫順，自處以禮，奉敬公主，內外諧穆，清河王懌親而重之。

translations.literal: Baoyin's disposition and nature were gentle and compliant; he placed himself within ritual, revered and respected the princess, and inside and outside were sheltered in harmony; Prince of Qinghe Yi was kin and valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle and compliant by nature, Baoyin conducted himself with ritual propriety and revered the princess. Household and court were at peace, and Prince Yi of Qinghe, as a kinsman, prized him.

sentences.zh: 永平四年，盧昶克蕭衍朐山戍，以琅邪戍主傅文驥守之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongping, Lu Chang took Liang's Zhushan garrison; Langye garrison chief Fu Wenji was put to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongping year 4 Lu Chang captured Liang's Zhushan garrison and put Langye garrison chief Fu Wenji in charge of its defense.

sentences.zh: 衍遣師攻文驥，盧昶督眾軍救之，詔寶夤為使持節、假安南將軍、別將，長驅往赴，受盧昶節度。

translations.literal: Yan sent troops to attack Wenji; Lu Chang supervised the mass of armies to rescue him; an edict made Baoyin Commissioner with credentials, acting General Who Pacifies the South, and separate commander, to drive straight and hurry to the rescue, subject to Lu Chang's command.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan sent troops against Wenji. Lu Chang led the relief force, and Baoyin was ordered as Commissioner with credentials, acting General Who Pacifies the South, and detached commander to ride hard to the rescue under Lu Chang's command.

sentences.zh: 賜帛三百匹，世宗於東堂餞之。

translations.literal: Three hundred bolts of silk were granted; Emperor Xuanwu feasted him farewell at the eastern hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted three hundred bolts of silk, and Emperor Xuanwu gave him a farewell feast in the eastern hall.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「蕭衍送死，連兵再離寒暑，卿忠規內挺，孝誠外亮，必欲鞭尸吳墓，戮衍江陰，故授卿以總統之任，仗卿以克捷之規，宜其勉歟？

translations.literal: An edict said: "Xiao Yan seeks his death; he has kept troops in the field through two rounds of cold and heat; you, loyal plan inwardly upright, filial sincerity outwardly bright, surely wish to whip the corpse at the Wu tomb and slay Yan on the southern bank of the Yangtze — therefore I entrust you with the overall command and rely on you for the plan of victory; you should strive, should you not?
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Xiao Yan is courting destruction. His armies have been in the field through two seasons. Your loyalty burns within and your filial devotion shines without; you surely mean to whip the corpse at the Wu tomb and slay Yan south of the Yangtze. I therefore entrust you with overall command and rely on you for victory. Strive on!

sentences.zh: 」寶夤對曰：「讎耻未復，枕戈俟旦，雖無申包之志，敢忘伍胥之心。

translations.literal: " Baoyin answered: "My feud shame is not yet avenged; I sleep on my spear awaiting dawn; though I lack Shen Baoxu's resolve, how dare I forget Wu Zixu's heart!
translations.idiomatic: " Baoyin answered, "My shame is not yet avenged; I sleep on my spear awaiting dawn. Though I lack Shen Baoxu's resolve, I dare not forget Wu Zixu's hatred.

sentences.zh: 今仰仗神謀，俯厲將帥，誓必拉彼姦勁，以清王略。

translations.literal: Now relying on your divine plan, and bending to encourage the generals and commanders, I swear I shall overthrow that villain's strength and clear the royal strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Now, relying on your wise strategy and spurring my commanders onward, I swear to crush that villain's power and restore the imperial design.

sentences.zh: 聖澤下臨，不勝悲荷。

translations.literal: Your sacred grace descends upon me; I cannot bear the grieving gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Your grace overwhelms me; I am overcome with grateful sorrow.

sentences.zh: 」因泣涕橫流，哽咽良久。

translations.literal: " Thereupon tears streamed across his face and he choked for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: " He then wept freely and choked with emotion for a long while.

sentences.zh: 於後，盧昶軍敗，唯寶夤全師而歸。

translations.literal: Afterwards Lu Chang's army was defeated; only Baoyin returned with his army intact.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lu Chang's army was defeated, but Baoyin returned with his force intact.

sentences.zh: 延昌初，除安東將軍、瀛州刺史，復其齊王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanchang he was made General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Ying Province, and his title as Prince of Qi was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yanchang era he was made General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Ying Province, and his title as Prince of Qi was restored.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷撫軍將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was moved to General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 及大乘賊起，寶夤遣軍討之，頻為賊破。

translations.literal: When the Mahayana rebels rose, Baoyin dispatched armies to attack them and was repeatedly defeated by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When the Mahayana rebels rose, Baoyin sent troops against them but was repeatedly defeated.

sentences.zh: 臺軍至，乃滅之。

translations.literal: When the metropolitan army arrived, they were then destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army arrived, the rebels were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，還京師。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling held court and he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling held court, he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍遣其將康絢於浮山堰淮以灌揚徐。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan dispatched his general Kang Xuan to dam the Huai at Fushan so as to flood Yang and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan sent his general Kang Xuan to build a dam on the Huai at Mount Fu in order to flood Yang and Xu.

sentences.zh: 除寶夤使持節、都督東討諸軍事、鎮東將軍以討之。

translations.literal: Baoyin was made Commissioner with credentials, Area Commander of the eastern punitive military affairs, and General Who Pacifies the East to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin was appointed Commissioner with credentials, commander of the eastern punitive armies, and General Who Pacifies the East to counter the threat.

sentences.zh: 尋復封梁郡開國公，寄食濟州之濮陽。

translations.literal: Soon he was again enfeoffed Duke of Liang Commandery and founding noble, with sustenance fief at Puyang in Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon re-enfeoffed as Duke of Liang Commandery, with his sustenance fief at Puyang in Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 熙平初，賊堰既成，淮水濫溢，將為揚徐之患，寶夤於堰上流，更鑿新渠，引注淮澤，水乃小減。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiping the rebel dam was already complete; the Huai River overflowed in flood; it was about to become a calamity for Yang and Xu; Baoyin upstream of the dam further dug a new canal, diverting flow into the Huai marshes, and the water then diminished somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiping era the dam was finished and the Huai flooded, threatening Yang and Xu. Baoyin dug a new canal upstream of the dam to divert water into the Huai marshes, and the flood subsided somewhat.

sentences.zh: 乃遣輕車將軍劉智文、虎威將軍劉延宗率壯士千餘，夜渡淮，燒其竹木營聚，破賊三壘，殺獲數千人，斬其直閤將軍王升明而還，火數日不滅。

translations.literal: He then dispatched General of Light Chariots Liu Zhiwen and General of Tiger Might Liu Yanzong to lead more than a thousand stalwart men, cross the Huai by night, burn their bamboo-and-wood camp clusters, break three rebel fortifications, kill and capture several thousand, behead their Direct Gate General Wang Shengming and return; the fire burned for several days without going out.
translations.idiomatic: He sent General of Light Chariots Liu Zhiwen and General of Tiger Might Liu Yanzong with more than a thousand stalwarts to cross the Huai by night, burn the enemy's bamboo-and-timber camps, storm three fortifications, kill and capture thousands, behead Direct Gate General Wang Shengming, and return. The fires burned for days.

sentences.zh: 衍將垣孟孫、張僧副等水軍三千，渡淮，北攻統軍呂叵。

translations.literal: Yan's generals Yuan Mengsun, Zhang Sengfu, and others with three thousand river troops crossed the Huai and attacked north against Area Commander Lu Po.
translations.idiomatic: Liang generals Yuan Mengsun and Zhang Sengfu crossed the Huai with three thousand river troops and attacked area commander Lu Po from the north.

sentences.zh: 寶夤遣府司馬元達、統軍魏續年等赴擊，破之，孟孫等奔退。

translations.literal: Baoyin dispatched the prefectural marshal Yuanda, area commander Wei Bunian, and others to go attack; they defeated them; Mengsun and the others fled in retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin sent his prefectural marshal Yuanda, area commander Wei Bunian, and others against them, routed the enemy, and Mengsun and his men fled.

sentences.zh: 乃授左光祿大夫、殿中尚書。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Left Grand Master of Splendor and Director Within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Left Grand Master of Splendor and Director Within the Palace.

sentences.zh: 寶夤又遣軍主周恭叔率壯士數百，夜渡淮南，焚賊徐州刺史張豹子等十一營，賊眾驚擾，自殺害者甚眾。

translations.literal: Baoyin again dispatched detachment commander Zhou Gongshu leading several hundred stalwart men; by night they crossed south of the Huai, burned eleven camps of the rebel Inspector of Xuzhou Zhang Baozi and others; the rebel masses were alarmed and thrown into disorder; very many killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin again sent detachment commander Zhou Gongshu with several hundred stalwarts to cross the Huai by night and burn eleven camps belonging to the rebel Inspector of Xuzhou Zhang Baozi and others. The rebel troops panicked, and many took their own lives.

sentences.zh: 寶夤還京師，又除使持節、散騎常侍、都督荊□東洛三州諸軍事、衞將軍、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Baoyin returned to the capital; he was again appointed Commissioner with credentials, Ordinary Cavalry Attendant, Area Commander over the military affairs of the three provinces of Jing□, Dongluo, Guard General, and Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin returned to the capital he was again appointed Commissioner with credentials, Ordinary Cavalry Attendant, area commander of military affairs for Jing□, Dongluo, and the third province, Guard General, and Inspector of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 不行，復為殿中尚書。

translations.literal: He did not go; he was again made Director Within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He did not take up the post and was again made Director Within the Palace.

sentences.zh: 寶夤之在淮堰，蕭衍手書與寶夤曰：「謝齊建安王寶夤。

translations.literal: While Baoyin was at the Huai embankment, Xiao Yan wrote him a personal letter, saying: "To Prince Jian'an of Qi, Baoyin.
translations.idiomatic: While Baoyin was at the Huai embankment, Xiao Yan wrote him a personal letter that began: "To Prince Jian'an of Qi, Baoyin.

sentences.zh: 亡兄長沙宣武王，昔投漢中，值北寇華陽，地絕一隅，內無素畜，外絕繼援，守危疏勒，計踰田單，卒能全土破敵，以弱為強。

translations.literal: My late elder brother, Prince Xuanwu of Changsha, once went to Hanzhong; he met northern invaders at Huayang; the land was cut off in a corner; within there were no stored provisions; without there was no continuing relief; defending in peril like Kashgar, plans surpassing Tian Dan—in the end he was able to preserve the land and defeat the enemy, turning weakness into strength.
translations.idiomatic: My late elder brother, Prince Xuanwu of Changsha, once withdrew to Hanzhong when northerners raided Huayang. Cornered on a scrap of land with no stores within and no relief from without, he held on as precariously as Kashgar and schemed more boldly than Tian Dan, yet in the end preserved his territory, routed the enemy, and turned weakness into strength.

sentences.zh: 使至之日，君臣動色，左右相賀，齊明帝每念此功，未嘗不輟箸咨嗟。

translations.literal: On the day the envoy arrived, ruler and ministers changed color; attendants left and right congratulated one another; Emperor Ming of Qi, whenever he recalled this achievement, never failed to lay down his chopsticks and sigh in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy arrived, court and emperor alike were moved; those around them exchanged congratulations. Whenever Emperor Ming of Qi recalled the feat, he would set down his chopsticks and sigh.

sentences.zh: 及至張永、崔慧景事，大將覆軍於外，小將懷貳於內，事危累卵，勢過綴旒。

translations.literal: When it came to the affairs of Zhang Yong and Cui Huijing, the great general lost his army outside; lesser generals harbored disloyalty within; the affair was as perilous as piled eggs; the situation surpassed a dangling kingly tassel.
translations.idiomatic: Then came the crises of Zhang Yong and Cui Huijing: a senior commander destroyed abroad, junior officers wavering at home—the realm balanced like a stack of eggs, the throne more precarious than a crown on a loose knot.

sentences.zh: 亡兄忠勇奮發，旋師大峴，重圍累日，一鼓魚潰，克定慧景，功踰桓文。

translations.literal: My late elder brother, loyal and brave, stirred himself; he turned the army at Great Xian; for days the heavy siege pressed; one drumbeat and they scattered like fish; he captured and settled Huijing; merit surpassing Duke Huan and Duke Wen.
translations.idiomatic: My late brother rallied with loyal courage, wheeled his army at Great Xian, broke a prolonged siege at a single drumbeat, and crushed Huijing—an achievement surpassing even Duke Huan and Duke Wen.

sentences.zh: 亡弟衞尉，兄弟勠力，盡心內外。

translations.literal: My late younger brother, the Guard Commandant—we brothers joined our strength and gave our hearts within and without.
translations.idiomatic: My late younger brother, the Guard Commandant, and I joined forces and gave our all at court and in the field.

sentences.zh: 大勳不報，翻罹荼酷，百口幽執，禍害相尋。

translations.literal: Great merit went unrewarded; instead they suffered bitter cruelty; a hundred mouths were imprisoned; calamity followed calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Great service went unrewarded; instead our house suffered cruel persecution— a hundred kin imprisoned, disaster heaped upon disaster.

sentences.zh: 朕於齊明帝，外有龕敵之力，內盡帷幄之誠，日自三省，曾無寸咎，遠身邊外，亦復不免。

translations.literal: I toward Emperor Ming of Qi outwardly had strength to hold the enemy at bay; inwardly fully devoted stratagem in the tent; daily I examined myself thrice; never a hair's fault; yet removing myself far to the outer borders, still I could not escape.
translations.idiomatic: Toward Emperor Ming of Qi I gave him every outward strength against his foes and every inward counsel in his councils. I examined myself thrice daily and was without fault, yet even when I kept far from court I could not escape harm.

sentences.zh: 遂遣劉山陽輕舟西上，來見掩襲。

translations.literal: Then he dispatched Liu Shanyang in light boats westward to come and make a surprise attack.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Liu Shanyang upriver in light boats to seize and strike at me.

sentences.zh: 時危事迫，勢不得已。

translations.literal: The times were perilous and affairs urgent; the situation left no choice.
translations.idiomatic: The hour was desperate and left me no choice.

sentences.zh: 所以誓眾樊鄧，會踰孟津，本欲翦除梅虫兒、茹法珍等，以雪冤酷，拔濟親屬，反身素里。

translations.literal: Therefore I swore the multitude at Fan and Deng and met beyond Meng Ford; the original intent was to cut down Mei Chong'er, Ru Fazhen, and others, to wipe away bitter wrongs, pull out and rescue kin, and return to one's native village.
translations.idiomatic: So I rallied the hosts at Fan and Deng and crossed beyond Meng Ford, intending to cut down Mei Chong'er, Ru Fazhen, and their ilk, avenge our wrongs, rescue our kin, and return home.

sentences.zh: 屬張稷、王珍國已建大事，寶晊、子晉屢動危機，迫樂推之心，應上天之命，事不獲已，豈其始願。

translations.literal: When Zhang Ji and Wang Zhenguo had already accomplished the great deed, Baozhi and Zijin repeatedly stirred crisis; pressed by hearts eager to elevate me, responding to Heaven's mandate—the affair could not be avoided; how could that have been my original wish?
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhang Ji and Wang Zhenguo had already set the great deed in motion, and Baozhi and Zijin repeatedly pushed the crisis forward, I was driven by those who wished to elevate me and answered what seemed Heaven's command. The throne was not what I had first sought.

sentences.zh: 所以自有天下，絕棄房室，斷除滋味，正欲使四海見其本心耳。

translations.literal: Therefore since possessing the realm I have abandoned wife and rooms and cut off delicacies—precisely wishing to let all within the four seas see my true heart.
translations.idiomatic: That is why, since taking the throne, I have forsaken my household and renounced delicacies—so that all under heaven might see my true heart.

sentences.zh: 勿謂今日之位，是為可重，朕之視此，曾不如一芥。

translations.literal: Do not think today's position is something weighty; I view this as not equal even to one mustard seed.
translations.idiomatic: Do not imagine that the throne today is something weighty; to me it is worth less than a mustard seed.

sentences.zh: 雖復崆峒之蹤難追，汾陽之志何遠。

translations.literal: Though the tracks of Ku Kong cannot be chased, how far off is the will of Fen Yang?
translations.idiomatic: Though one cannot recover the abdication of the Yellow Emperor on Mount Kongtong, how distant is the renunciation of Guo Ziyi of Fenyang?

sentences.zh: 而今立此堰，卿當未達本意。

translations.literal: Yet now in building this embankment, you perhaps have not yet grasped my true intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in building this embankment now, you have perhaps not yet understood my true intent.

sentences.zh: 朕於昆蟲，猶不欲殺，亦何急爭無用之地，戰蒼生之命也！

translations.literal: I toward insects still do not wish to kill—how urgent is it to contest useless land and battle over the lives of the common people!
translations.idiomatic: I would not willingly kill even an insect—why then rush to fight over worthless ground and wager the lives of the people!

sentences.zh: 正為李繼伯在壽陽，侵犯邊境，歲月滋甚。

translations.literal: It is precisely because Li Jibo is at Shouyang, encroaching on the border—month by month it grows worse.
