translations.idiomatic: It is only because Li Jibo at Shouyang has been encroaching on the frontier, and the raids grow worse month by month.

sentences.zh: 或攻小城小戍，或掠一村一里。

translations.literal: Sometimes attacking small cities and small garrisons; sometimes raiding one village or one li.
translations.idiomatic: One day he strikes a minor fort, the next he plunders a hamlet or village.

sentences.zh: 若小相酬答，終無寧日，邊邑爭桑，吳楚連禍。

translations.literal: If we answered each small insult, there would never be a day of peace; border towns would fight over mulberry trees; Wu and Chu would suffer linked calamity.
translations.idiomatic: If we traded blow for petty blow, peace would never come; frontier towns would quarrel over mulberry groves, and Wu and Chu would share one endless disaster.

sentences.zh: 所以每抑鎮戍，不與校計。

translations.literal: Therefore I always restrained the frontier garrisons and did not settle accounts with them.
translations.idiomatic: So I repeatedly held the frontier garrisons back and refused to answer in kind.

sentences.zh: 繼伯既得如此，濫竊彌多。

translations.literal: Jibo having gotten to this point, wanton seizure grew ever more.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jibo saw he could go this far, his depredations only multiplied.

sentences.zh: 今修此堰，止欲以報繼伯侵盜之役，既非大舉，所以不復文移北土。

translations.literal: Now in repairing this embankment I only wish to repay Jibo's raids and plunder; since it is not a major campaign, therefore I do not again send official dispatches to the northern land.
translations.idiomatic: I am building this embankment only to answer Jibo's raids and plunder. It is no full-scale war, which is why I have not sent formal dispatches to the north.

sentences.zh: 卿幼有倜儻之心，早懷縱橫之氣。

translations.literal: You from youth had a bold and unrestrained heart; early you harbored a spirit of bold stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: You have been bold and unbounded since youth, and long carried the temper of a strategist.

sentences.zh: 往日卿於石頭舉事，雖不克捷，亦丈夫也。

translations.literal: On former days when you at Shitou raised the affair—though you did not achieve victory, still you were a true man.
translations.idiomatic: When you raised your banner at Shitou in days past you did not prevail, yet even so you showed yourself a man.

sentences.zh: 今止河洛，真其時矣。

translations.literal: Now blocking the He and Luo—truly this is the time for it.
translations.idiomatic: The He and Luo region lies open now—truly the moment is yours.

sentences.zh: 雖然，為卿計者，莫若行率此眾，襲據彭城，別當遣軍以相影援。

translations.literal: Even so, for you the best plan is none other than to lead this army straight away, strike and seize Pengcheng; separately I will dispatch troops to shadow and support you.
translations.idiomatic: Still, your best course is to lead these troops at once, strike, and seize Pengcheng; I will send another force to support you from afar.

sentences.zh: 得捷之後，便遣卿兄子屏侍送卿國廟、并卿室家及諸姪從。

translations.literal: After victory, I will dispatch your elder brother's son Ping Shi to escort your state temple, together with your wife and household and your various nephews to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Once you prevail, I will send your brother's son Ping Shi to escort your ancestral temple, your household, and your nephews to join you.

sentences.zh: 若方欲還北，更設奇計，恐機事一差，難重復集，勿為韓信，受困野鷄。

translations.literal: If you still wish to return north and set up another stratagem, I fear one slip in timing cannot be gathered again—do not become Han Xin, trapped by the wild cock.
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to turn north again and try some new scheme, one missed chance may never return—do not become another Han Xin, caught like a bird in the wild-cock snare.

sentences.zh: 」寶夤表送其書，陳其忿毒之意。

translations.literal: " Baoyin memorialized forwarding the letter, stating its resentful and venomous intent.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin forwarded the letter in a memorial, denouncing its spiteful tone.

sentences.zh: 朝廷為之報答。

translations.literal: The court made a reply on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: The court drafted a reply on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 寶夤志存雪復，屢請居邊。

translations.literal: Baoyin aspired to wipe away wrongs and recover; repeatedly he requested to serve on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin burned to avenge his wrongs and repeatedly asked to serve on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 神龜中，出為都督徐南兗二州諸軍事、車騎將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: During Shengui, he went out as Area Commander of the military affairs of the two provinces Xu and Southern Yan, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shengui era he was sent out as area commander of military affairs for Xu and Southern Yan, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 乃起學館於清東，朔望引見土姓子弟，接以恩顏，與論經義，勤於政治，吏民愛之。

translations.literal: He then raised an academy east of Qing; on the first and fifteenth of each month he summoned sons and nephews of local gentry, received them with gracious countenance, and discussed the classics with them; diligent in governance; officials and people loved him.
translations.idiomatic: He founded a school east of Qing and, on the first and fifteenth of each month, received local gentry's sons with warm courtesy and debated the classics with them. Diligent in administration, he won the affection of officials and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 凡在三州，皆著名稱。

translations.literal: Whenever in the three provinces, he was famed and praised.
translations.idiomatic: In each of the three provinces where he served, he won renown.

sentences.zh: 正光二年，徵為車騎大將軍、尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengguang, he was summoned as General of Chariots and Cavalry and Left Vice Minister of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengguang he was recalled as General of Chariots and Cavalry and Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 善於吏職，甚有聲名。

translations.literal: Skilled in official duties; very renowned.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in administration and widely respected.

sentences.zh: 四年，上表曰：

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 臣聞堯典有黜陟之文，周書有考績之法，雖其源難得而尋，然條流抑亦可知矣。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the Canon of Yao contains texts on dismissal and promotion; the Documents of Zhou contain methods of examining achievement—though their sources are hard to trace, yet their branches and currents may still be known.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the Canon of Yao sets out rules for promotion and demotion, and the Documents of Zhou lay down methods for assessing performance. Though their origins are obscure, their principles can still be discerned.

sentences.zh: 大較在于官人用才，審於所莅；

translations.literal: In the main it lies in the state employing men according to talent and examining closely what they oversee;
translations.idiomatic: In essence it comes down to appointing men for their talents and judging them by the offices they hold;

sentences.zh: 練迹校名，驗於虛實。

translations.literal: refining traces and checking names, verifying against emptiness and reality.
translations.idiomatic: refining their records, testing their reputations, and verifying deed against claim.

sentences.zh: 豈不以臧否得之餘論，優劣著於歷試者乎？

translations.literal: Is it not because praise and blame are obtained from further discussion, and superiority and inferiority are fixed by repeated trials?
translations.idiomatic: Are not merit and fault settled only after repeated scrutiny, and rank and failure decided only after repeated trial?

sentences.zh: 既聲窮於月旦，品定於黃紙，用效於名輩，事彰於臺閤，則賞罰之途，差有商準；

translations.literal: Once reputation is exhausted at the monthly review, rank fixed on yellow paper, effect tested among named peers, and deeds displayed at the Secretariat, then the path of reward and punishment has some standard to weigh;
translations.idiomatic: Once monthly appraisals have exhausted a man's reputation, yellow-edict ranks have fixed his grade, peers have tested his results, and the Secretariat has recorded his deeds, reward and punishment at least have some measure;

sentences.zh: 用捨之宜，非無依據。

translations.literal: the fitness of employment and dismissal is not without basis.
translations.idiomatic: and appointment and removal are not wholly arbitrary.

sentences.zh: 雖復勇進忘退之儔，奔競於市里；

translations.literal: Though again there are those who, brave in advance and forgetting retreat, rush and compete in the market lanes;
translations.idiomatic: Even those who push forward relentlessly and scramble in the streets,

sentences.zh: 過分亡涯之請，馳騖於多門；

translations.literal: requests beyond measure and without bounds gallop through many gates;
translations.idiomatic: and those whose demands know no limit and who petition at every door,

sentences.zh: 猶且顧其聲第，慎其與奪。

translations.literal: still they look to their reputation and rank and are careful about what is given and taken away.
translations.idiomatic: still watch their standing and rank and weigh what may be granted or withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 器分定於下，爵位懸於上，不可妄叨故也。

translations.literal: Capacity and rank are fixed below; titles and positions hang above—one must not presumptuously usurp, therefore.
translations.idiomatic: Office and rank are defined below and titles suspended above; one must not seize them unworthily.

sentences.zh: 今竊見考功之典，所懷未喻，敢竭無隱，試陳萬一。

translations.literal: Now I have privately seen the canon of examining achievement; what it embodies I have not understood; I dare exhaust concealment and venture to set forth one part in ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the examination system as I have observed it, the intent escapes me. Allow me to speak plainly and offer what little I can.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this?

sentences.zh: 竊惟文武之名，在人之極地；

translations.literal: I privately consider that the names of civil and military achievement are the utmost ground of a man;
translations.idiomatic: I believe that the titles of civil and military merit mark the highest ground a man can stand on;

sentences.zh: 德行之稱，為生之最首。

translations.literal: the designation of virtue and conduct is the foremost of life's honors.
translations.idiomatic: and the name for virtue and conduct is the first honor in life.

sentences.zh: 忠貞之美，立朝之譽，仁義之號，處身之端，自非職惟九官，任當四岳，授曰爾諧，讓稱俞往，將何以克厭大名，允茲令問。

translations.literal: The beauty of loyalty and steadfastness, the reputation of standing at court, the title of benevolence and righteousness, the upright bearing of personal conduct—unless one's office is among the nine ministers and one's charge equals the four mountain lords, with appointment saying 'you harmonize' and yielding called 'I go'—how could one fulfill these great names and truly merit such fine repute?
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty, public honor, benevolence, and upright conduct are not titles one can truly bear unless one holds one of the great offices of state and is appointed with the gravity due a chief minister. How then can every man claim such names and deserve such praise?

sentences.zh: 自比已來，官罔高卑，人無貴賤，皆飾辭假說，用相褒舉。

translations.literal: Since recent times, regardless of office high or low and person noble or base, all adorn words and borrow talk, using them to praise and recommend one another.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times, high and low, noble and base alike polish phrases and trade flattery, praising one another without end.

sentences.zh: 涇渭同波，薰猶共器，求者不能量其多少，與者不復覈其是非。

translations.literal: The Jing and Wei share one wave; orchid and stinkweed share one vessel; seekers cannot measure how much there is; givers no longer verify what is right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Clear and foul run in one stream, fragrant and foul sit in one bowl; those who seek favor cannot tell how much is offered, and those who grant it no longer ask what is true.

sentences.zh: 遂使冠履相貿，名與實爽，謂之考功，事同汎陟，紛紛漫漫，焉可勝言。

translations.literal: Thus cap and shoe are mutually traded; name and reality diverge; calling it examination of achievement, the affair is like a general promotion; confused and boundless—how can it all be told?
translations.idiomatic: Cap and sandal change places; name and fact part company. What is called examination of merit becomes mere blanket promotion—confusion beyond telling.

sentences.zh: 又在京之官，積年一考。

translations.literal: Again, for officials in the capital, achievement is examined once accumulated over years.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital, moreover, officials are reviewed only once every few years.

sentences.zh: 其中或所事之主遷移數四，或所奉之君身名廢絕，或具僚離索，或同事凋零，雖當時文簿，記其殿最，日久月深，駁落都盡，人有去留，誰復掌其勤墮？

translations.literal: Among them, some masters they served were transferred several times over; some lords they served had their persons and names extinguished; some fellow officials were scattered; some colleagues withered away; though at the time documents recorded their grades of achievement, as days grew long and months deep the records fell away entirely; men came and went—who again kept charge of their diligence and slackness?
translations.idiomatic: Some served several masters in succession; some served lords who fell and vanished; colleagues dispersed or died. Though records once noted each man's grade, the papers decayed with time, and as men came and went, who still tracked who had worked and who had slacked?

sentences.zh: 或停休積稔，或分隔數千，累年之後，方求追訪聲迹，立其考第。

translations.literal: Some stopped and rested for accumulated years, or were separated by several thousand li; after accumulated years they then sought to trace reputation and deeds and establish their examination rank.
translations.idiomatic: Some were idle for years on end, or separated by thousands of li; only after many years did anyone try to reconstruct reputations and set examination ranks.

sentences.zh: 無不苟相悅附，共為脣齒，飾垢掩疵，妄加丹素，趣令得階而已，無所顧惜。

translations.literal: None failed mutually to please and attach, together forming lip and tooth, adorning filth and covering blemishes, falsely adding cinnabar and plainness, hurrying only to obtain rank and nothing more, without any care.
translations.idiomatic: None failed to flatter one another, cover faults, paint mediocrity as brilliance, and seek promotion by any means, without scruple.

sentences.zh: 賢達君子，未免斯患；

translations.literal: Worthy and noble gentlemen cannot avoid this affliction;
translations.idiomatic: Even worthy and principled men are not spared;

sentences.zh: 中庸已降，夫復何論。

translations.literal: for those below the middling, what further is there to say?
translations.idiomatic: for the mediocre and worse, what need even to speak?

sentences.zh: 官以求成，身以請立，上下相蒙，莫斯為甚。

translations.literal: Office sought to succeed; person sought to stand; above and below mutually concealed—nothing exceeds this.
translations.idiomatic: Posts were sought by fraud and careers built on falsehood; superiors and subordinates deceived one another—and nothing went deeper.

sentences.zh: 又勤恤人隱，咸歸守令，厥任非輕，所責實重。

translations.literal: Again, diligent care for the people's hidden woes all returns to the prefects and magistrates; their charge is not light and the responsibility borne is truly heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Again, the people's hidden grievances are entrusted to prefects and magistrates—a burden neither light nor nominal.

sentences.zh: 然及其考課，悉以六載為程，既而限滿代還，復經六年而敍。

translations.literal: Yet when their achievements come to examination, all take six years as the term; when the term is full and they return in replacement, another six years pass before promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when they are reviewed, the cycle is six years; when a term ends and they are replaced, another six years pass before rank advances.

sentences.zh: 是則歲周十二，始得一階。

translations.literal: Thus twelve years complete before one rank is obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve years must pass before they gain a single step in rank.

sentences.zh: 於東西兩省、文武閑職、公府散佐、無事冗官，或數旬方應一直，或朔望止於暫朝，及其考日，更得四年為限。

translations.literal: For the eastern and western provinces, civil and military idle posts, public-office staff without fixed duties, and officials with nothing to do, some respond to one shift only after several tens of days; some attend court only briefly on new and full moon; when examination day comes, they again get four years as the limit.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the two capital provinces, in idle civil and military posts, in staff and sinecure offices, some report for duty only once in many weeks and attend court briefly at the new and full moon; when review comes, their term is only four years.

sentences.zh: 是則一紀之中，便登三級。

translations.literal: Thus within one twelve-year cycle they may ascend three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In a single twelve-year span they may rise three ranks.

sentences.zh: 彼以實勞劇任，而遷貴之路至難；

translations.literal: Those, by real toil and heavy charge, find the road to advancement and honor extremely hard;
translations.idiomatic: Those who bear real labor and heavy responsibility find the path to honor all but closed;

sentences.zh: 此以散位虛名，而升陟之方甚易。

translations.literal: these, by empty rank and nominal title, find the method of ascent very easy.
translations.idiomatic: while those with hollow titles and empty posts find promotion easy.

sentences.zh: 何內外之相懸，令厚薄之如是！

translations.literal: How inner and outer are so far apart; how reward and burden are thus unequal!
translations.idiomatic: What a gulf between inside and outside; what a skew between burden and reward!

sentences.zh: 又聞之，聖人大寶曰位，何以守位曰仁。

translations.literal: I have also heard that the sage's great treasure is called position; what preserves position is called benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that the sage's greatest treasure is office, and that what preserves office is benevolence.

sentences.zh: 孟子亦曰：仁義忠信天爵也，公卿大夫人爵也。

translations.literal: Mencius also said: Benevolence, righteousness, loyalty, and good faith are Heaven's rank; duke, minister, grandee, and man are man's rank.
translations.idiomatic: Mencius also said: 'Benevolence, righteousness, loyalty, and good faith are Heaven's nobility; the ranks of duke, minister, and grandee are man's nobility.'

sentences.zh: 古之人修其天爵而人爵從之。

translations.literal: The men of old cultivated Heaven's rank and man's rank followed.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients cultivated Heaven's nobility, and human rank followed of itself.

sentences.zh: 故雖文質異時，污隆殊世，莫不寶茲名器，不以假人。

translations.literal: Therefore though civil and substance differ in age and decline and ascent differ in era, none failed to treasure these names and vessels and not lend them to others.
translations.idiomatic: So though ages differ in culture and fortune, none failed to treat these titles as treasures and refuse to lend them lightly.

sentences.zh: 是以賞罰之柄，恒自持也。

translations.literal: Thus the handle of reward and punishment was constantly held in one's own hand.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the power to reward and punish remained firmly in the ruler's own hand.

sentences.zh: 至乃周之藹藹，五叔無官；

translations.literal: Even to the flourishing Zhou, the five uncles had no office;
translations.idiomatic: Even in flourishing Zhou the five royal uncles held no office;

sentences.zh: 漢之察察，館陶徒請。

translations.literal: in scrutinizing Han, the Prince of Guantao asked in vain.
translations.idiomatic: and in austere Han even the Prince of Guantao's petition was denied.

sentences.zh: 豈不重骨肉、私親親？

translations.literal: Was it not because they valued flesh and bone and favored kin?
translations.idiomatic: Was this not because rulers cherished kin?

sentences.zh: 誠以賞罰一差，則無以懲勸；

translations.literal: Truly because one error in reward and punishment then there is no means to admonish and encourage;
translations.idiomatic: Yes—but also because one skew in reward and punishment destroys all incentive;

sentences.zh: 至公暫替，則覬覦相欺。

translations.literal: when supreme fairness is briefly set aside, then covetous watching and mutual deception follow.
translations.idiomatic: and when perfect fairness wavers, envy and deceit follow.

sentences.zh: 故至慎至惜，殷勤若此。

translations.literal: Therefore utmost caution, utmost sparing—earnest as this.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the utmost caution, the utmost restraint.

sentences.zh: 況乎親非胏腑，才乖秀逸；

translations.literal: How much more when kin is not flesh from the belly and talent departs from excellence;
translations.idiomatic: How much more when the beneficiary is no close kinsman and talent falls short of distinction;

sentences.zh: 或充單介之使，始無汗馬之勞；

translations.literal: some fill a solitary envoy's mission yet from the start have no sweat-of-the-horse labor;
translations.idiomatic: when some serve a minor embassy without ever sweating over campaign or horse;

sentences.zh: 或說興利之規，終慚十一之潤。

translations.literal: some speak plans to increase profit yet in the end are ashamed before an eleven-part gain.
translations.idiomatic: when others propose profit schemes yet cannot show even a tenth part's return.

sentences.zh: 皆虛張無功，妄指贏益，坐獲數階之官，藉成通顯之貴。

translations.literal: All falsely spread empty achievement, falsely point to surplus and gain, sit and obtain several ranks of office, and borrow their way to passing eminence and honor.
translations.idiomatic: All inflate hollow merit, claim false profit, collect rank after rank, and ride borrowed glory to prominence.

sentences.zh: 於是巧詐萌生，偽辯鋒出，役萬慮以求榮，開百方而逐利。

translations.literal: Then crafty fraud sprouted; false debate flashed forth; they deployed ten thousand schemes to seek glory and opened a hundred paths to chase profit.
translations.idiomatic: Then deceit flourished, sophistry sharpened, and men deployed every scheme for honor and every path to profit.

sentences.zh: 握樞秉鈞者，亦知其若斯，[7]但抑之則其流已注，引之則有何紀極。

translations.literal: Those who grasp the pivot and hold the balance also know it is like this, [7] but to suppress it then its flow has already poured forth; to draw it forth then what limit is there?
translations.idiomatic: Those who hold power know this as well, [7] yet to dam the flood is already too late, and to let it run is to lose all bounds.

sentences.zh: 夫琴瑟在於必和，更張求其適調。

translations.literal: The zither and se must harmonize; one restrings to seek proper tuning.
translations.idiomatic: As zither and lute must be tuned together, so strings must be reset to find the right pitch.

sentences.zh: 去者既不可追，來者猶或宜改。

translations.literal: What has gone cannot be pursued; what is coming may still be fit to change.
translations.idiomatic: The past cannot be recovered, but what lies ahead may still be amended.

sentences.zh: 按周官太宰之職：歲終，則令官府各正所司，受其會計，聽其致事，而詔於王；

translations.literal: According to the office of the Grand Minister in the Offices of Zhou: at year's end he then ordered each office to rectify what it administered, receive its accounts, hear its report of affairs, and announce to the king;
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Zhou charge the Grand Minister: at year's end he orders each office to correct its administration, submit accounts, report its business, and lay all before the king;

sentences.zh: 三歲，則大計羣吏之治而誅賞之。

translations.literal: At three years he then broadly reckons the governance of the multitude of officials and punishes and rewards them.
translations.idiomatic: and every three years he reviews all officials' governance and metes out punishment and reward.

sentences.zh: 愚謂：今可粗依其準，見居官者，每歲終，本曹皆明辨在官日月，具覈才行能否，審其實用而注其上下，游辭宕說，無一取焉。

translations.literal: I foolishly propose: now one may roughly follow that standard; for those presently in office, at each year's end their original bureau should all clearly distinguish months and days in office, fully verify ability and conduct and whether they can perform, examine their real utility and note them above or below—wandering words and idle talk, not one to be taken.
translations.idiomatic: I propose that we follow that model in broad outline: each year every bureau should record clearly how long each official has served, assess ability and conduct without flattery, judge real performance, and mark each man high or low—accepting no glib excuse.

sentences.zh: 列上尚書，覆其合否。

translations.literal: Arrange and submit to the Imperial Secretariat; review whether they accord or not.
translations.idiomatic: Submit the lists to the Secretariat for verification.

sentences.zh: 如有紕謬，即正而罰之，不得方復推詰委否，容其進退。

translations.literal: If there are errors, then correct and punish them; one must not again push inquiry and delegate yes-or-no, allowing advance and retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Where there is error, correct it and punish it; do not again defer judgment, shift responsibility, and let offenders slip away.

sentences.zh: 既定其優劣，善惡交分。

translations.literal: Once their superiority and inferiority are fixed, good and evil are clearly distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Once rank and merit are fixed, the worthy and unworthy stand clearly apart.

sentences.zh: 庸短下第，黜凡以明法；

translations.literal: Mediocre and deficient are ranked last; the ordinary are dismissed to clarify the law;
translations.idiomatic: Place the mediocre and deficient at the bottom of the list, dismiss the unremarkable to make the law plain;

sentences.zh: 幹務忠清，甄能以記賞。

translations.literal: Those who handle affairs with loyalty and integrity—select their ability to record reward.
translations.idiomatic: For those who serve with loyalty and integrity, select merit and record rewards.

sentences.zh: 總而奏之。

translations.literal: Compile in total and submit them.
translations.idiomatic: Compile the whole and submit it as a memorial.

sentences.zh: 經奏之後，考功曹別書於黃紙、油帛。

translations.literal: After it passes through memorial submission, the Merit Evaluation Bureau separately writes on yellow paper and oiled silk.
translations.idiomatic: After the memorial is submitted, the Merit Evaluation Bureau records separate copies on yellow paper and oiled silk.

sentences.zh: 一通則本曹尚書與令、僕印署，留於門下；

translations.literal: One copy then—the bureau head Secretary seals with the Minister and Vice-Minister, kept at the Gate Department;
translations.idiomatic: One copy is sealed by the bureau's Secretary together with the Minister and Vice-Minister of the Secretariat and kept at the Gate Department;

sentences.zh: 一通則以侍中、黃門印署，掌在尚書。

translations.literal: One copy then is sealed by the Attendant-in-Ordinary and Yellow Gate, held in charge by the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The other is sealed by the Attendant-in-Ordinary and the Yellow Gate Director and held by the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 嚴加緘密，不得開視，考績之日，然後對共裁量。

translations.literal: Strictly sealed tight, may not be opened for viewing; on the day of merit evaluation, then opened facing each other for joint deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Both are sealed strictly and must not be opened beforehand; only on evaluation day are they brought out and weighed together.

sentences.zh: 如此，則少存實錄，薄止姦回。

translations.literal: Thus, then truth is slightly preserved and fraud somewhat checked.
translations.idiomatic: In this way truth would be better preserved and fraud somewhat contained.

sentences.zh: 其內外考格，裁非庸管，乞求博議，以為畫一。

translations.literal: As for the internal and external evaluation standards, the decision is no mediocre oversight; I beg broad deliberation to make them uniform.
translations.idiomatic: The standards for internal and external evaluation are no petty matter; I beg wide deliberation to establish one uniform rule.

sentences.zh: 若殊謀異策，事關廢興，遐邇所談，物無異議者，自可臨時斟酌，匪拘恒例。

translations.literal: If extraordinary plans and different strategies concern ruin and rise, discussed far and near, with none dissenting, naturally one may weigh them at the time, not bound by constant precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Where a singular plan or strategy bears on the fate of the state, and men near and far discuss it without dissent, the court may weigh it at the moment and need not be bound by fixed precedent.

sentences.zh: 至如援流引比之訴，貪榮求級之請，如不限以關鍵，肆其傍通，則蔓草難除，涓流遂積，穢我彝章，撓茲大典。

translations.literal: As for appeals citing parallel cases and requests greedily seeking rank and grade—if not limited by key constraints and allowed free lateral access, then spreading weeds are hard to remove, trickles accumulate, defiling our great statutes and undermining these grand norms.
translations.idiomatic: But appeals that cite stray precedents and petitions driven by greed for rank—if not held in check, allowed to slip through side doors—will spread like weeds, accumulate drop by drop, and defile our statutes and undermine this great institution.

sentences.zh: 謂宜明加禁斷，以全至治，開返本之路，杜澆弊之門。

translations.literal: It is said one should clearly forbid and cut off, to preserve perfect governance, open the road back to fundamentals, and block the gate of decadent abuse.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that these should be plainly forbidden, to preserve good order, reopen the path to fundamentals, and shut the door to decay.

sentences.zh: 如斯，則吉士盈朝，薪槱載煥矣。

translations.literal: If thus, then good men fill the court, and firewood bundles blaze brilliantly.
translations.idiomatic: Then good men would fill the court, and worth would blaze like bundled kindling.

sentences.zh: 詔付外博議，以為永式，竟無所定。

translations.literal: An edict ordered outward broad deliberation as permanent form; in the end nothing was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent the proposal out for broad discussion as a permanent rule, but in the end nothing was settled.

sentences.zh: 時蕭衍弟子西豐侯正德來降，寶夤表曰：

translations.literal: At the time Xiao Yan's younger brother's son, the Marquis of Xifeng Zhengde, came to surrender; Baoyin submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xiao Yan's nephew, the Marquis of Xifeng, Zhengde, came over in surrender. Baoyin submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 伏見揚州表，蕭正德自云避禍，遠投宸掖，背父叛君，駭議眾口，深心指趣，厥情難測。

translations.literal: Humbly I have seen the Yangzhou report: Xiao Zhengde himself says he fled disaster and came from afar to the imperial side; he betrayed his father and rebelled against his lord—shocking all voices; his deep intent and direction—his feelings are hard to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: I have read the Yangzhou report. Xiao Zhengde claims he fled calamity and came from afar to the imperial court. He betrayed his father and turned against his lord—men everywhere are appalled. His deeper motives and inclinations are impossible to read.

sentences.zh: 臣聞立身行道，始於事親，終於事君。

translations.literal: I have heard that to establish oneself and walk the Way begins with serving parents and ends with serving the lord.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that to stand upright in the world and walk the Way one begins by serving one's parents and ends by serving one's ruler.

sentences.zh: 故君親盡之以恒敬，嚴父兼之以博愛。

translations.literal: Therefore lord and parents are served with constant reverence; the stern father is joined with broad love.
translations.idiomatic: Hence one serves ruler and parents with unchanging reverence, and honors a stern father with encompassing love.

sentences.zh: 斯人倫之所先，王教之盛典。

translations.literal: This is what human relations put first and the royal teaching's grand ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: This comes first among human relations and stands among the crowning rites of royal teaching.

sentences.zh: 三千之罪，莫大於不孝。

translations.literal: Among three thousand offenses, none is greater than unfiliality.
translations.idiomatic: Of the three thousand offenses, none is greater than unfilial conduct.

sentences.zh: 毀則藏姦，常刑靡赦。

translations.literal: Those who destroy filial bonds conceal wickedness; regular punishment never pardons.
translations.idiomatic: Those who destroy filial duty conceal treachery, and ordinary punishments know no pardon for them.

sentences.zh: 所以晉恭獲謗，無所逃死；

translations.literal: Therefore Duke Gong of Jin received slander and had nowhere to escape death;
translations.idiomatic: This is why Duke Gong of Jin, though slandered, could not escape death;

sentences.zh: 衞伋受誣，二子繼沒。

translations.literal: Wei Ji received false accusation, and his two sons died in succession.
translations.idiomatic: and why Wei Ji, though falsely accused, saw both his sons die in turn.

sentences.zh: 親命匪棄，國孰無父？

translations.literal: If a parent's command is not abandoned, which state lacks a father?
translations.idiomatic: If a father's charge is not cast aside, in what realm is there no father?

sentences.zh: 況今封豕尚存，長蛇未滅，偷生江表，自安毒酖。

translations.literal: Moreover, now the great boar still exists and the long snake is not yet destroyed; clinging to life south of the Yangtze, self-comforting in poison wine.
translations.idiomatic: And now the great enemy still lives and the long serpent is not yet destroyed, while he clings to life south of the Yangtze and rests easy in a cup of poison.

sentences.zh: 而正德居猶子之親，竊通侯之貴，父榮於國，子爵於家，履霜弗聞，去就先結。

translations.literal: Yet Zhengde occupies the status of a nephew-by-marriage, usurping a marquis's nobility; his father is honored in the state, he holds noble rank at home—he did not hear frost underfoot, and departure and approach were already decided.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhengde holds the standing of an heir-son, enjoys a stolen marquisate, sees his father honored by the state and himself ennobled at home, never felt the frost underfoot, and had already decided where to go and where to stay.

sentences.zh: 隔絕山淮，溫凊永盡，定省長違，報復何日？

translations.literal: Cut off by mountains and the Huai, warmth and coolness forever ended, regular visits to parents long violated—when to repay?
translations.idiomatic: Mountains and the Huai stand between them; he can no longer warm or cool his father's bed, no longer attend him morning and evening—when will he repay what he owes?

sentences.zh: 以此為心，心可知矣。

translations.literal: With this as his heart, the heart can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Take this as the measure of his heart, and his heart is plain enough.

sentences.zh: 皇朝綿基累葉，恩均四海，自北徂南，要荒仰澤，能言革化，無思不韙。

translations.literal: The imperial dynasty's foundation extends through many generations; grace fills the four seas; from north to south, distant wilds look up to its bounty; those who can speak are changed by its reform; no thought fails to accord.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty's foundations run through many generations; its grace reaches the four seas. From north to south, the farthest frontiers look up to its bounty; speech itself is remade by its transforming power, and no loyal thought falls out of accord.

sentences.zh: 賁玉帛於丘園，標忠孝以納賞；

translations.literal: Adorn jade and silk in garden-mounds; mark loyalty and filial piety to receive reward;
translations.idiomatic: Men bring jade and silk from their garden retreats and are rewarded for loyalty and filial piety;

sentences.zh: 築藳街于伊洛，集華裔其歸心。

translations.literal: Build a reed-hut street at Yi and Luo; gather Chinese descendants whose hearts return.
translations.idiomatic: reed-hut lanes are built at Yi and Luo, and Chinese exiles of every branch return with loyal hearts.

sentences.zh: 被髮鐻身之酋，屈膝而請吏；

translations.literal: Chieftains with disheveled hair and pierced bodies kneel and request officials;
translations.idiomatic: Chiefs with loose hair and pierced bodies kneel and ask to be made subjects;

sentences.zh: 交趾文身之渠，款關而効質。

translations.literal: Jiaozhi tattooed chieftains knock at the passes and offer hostages.
translations.idiomatic: and tattooed chieftains of Jiaozhi knock at the gates and present themselves as hostages.

sentences.zh: 至如正德，宜甄義以致貶。

translations.literal: As for Zhengde, one should examine righteousness to bring censure.
translations.idiomatic: A man like Zhengde ought to be judged by principle and held up for censure.

sentences.zh: 昔越栖會稽，賴宰嚭以獲立；

translations.literal: Formerly Yue dwelt at Kuaiji and relied on Grand Administrator Pi to gain establishment;
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Yue held to Kuaiji and owed its survival to Grand Administrator Pi;

sentences.zh: 漢困彭宋，實丁公而獲免。

translations.literal: Han was trapped at Peng and Song and indeed relied on Duke Ding to obtain escape.
translations.idiomatic: the Han was besieged at Pengcheng and Song and was saved through Duke Ding.

sentences.zh: 吳項已平，二臣即法。

translations.literal: Once Wu and Xiang were pacified, the two ministers immediately faced the law.
translations.idiomatic: Yet once Wu and Xiang were pacified, both men were brought to justice.

sentences.zh: 豈不錄其情哉？

translations.literal: Did the court not record their circumstances?
translations.idiomatic: Did the court fail to weigh their circumstances?

sentences.zh: 欲明責以示後。

translations.literal: It wished to clarify responsibility to show posterity.
translations.idiomatic: It wished to make responsibility plain for those who come after.

sentences.zh: 況遺君忽父，狼子是心，既不親親，安能親人。

translations.literal: Moreover, abandoning the lord and neglecting the father—the heart of a wolf-cub is his heart; since he does not treat kin as kin, how can he treat others as kin?
translations.idiomatic: All the more when he abandons his ruler and neglects his father: his heart is the heart of a wolf cub. If he will not love his own kin, how can he love anyone else?

sentences.zh: 中間變詐，或有萬等。

translations.literal: In between, treacherous changes—there may be ten thousand kinds.
translations.idiomatic: In the mean time his shifts and deceits may take ten thousand forms.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下聖敬自天，欽光纂歷，昭德塞違，以臨羣后，脫苞此凶醜，置之列位，百官是象，其何誅焉！

translations.literal: Humbly, Your Majesty's sage reverence comes from Heaven; you esteem glory and inherit the calendar; you display virtue and block transgression to oversee the multitude of lords—if you release and harbor this vicious ugliness and place him in the ranks, the hundred officials as model—how can one punish!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's sacred reverence comes from Heaven; you inherit the mandate with sober glory, display virtue and hold back wrongdoing, and rule over all the lords. If you now wrap up this wicked man and set him among the ranks—when all officials look to him as an example—how then can guilt be punished?

sentences.zh: 臣釁結禍深，痛纏肝髓，日暮途遙，復報無日，豈區區於一豎哉？

translations.literal: I, guilt-bound, disaster deep; pain winds through liver and marrow; sunset, the road far; revenge has no day—is it merely about one petty fellow?
translations.idiomatic: My guilt runs deep and disaster clings to me; grief coils through my liver and marrow. The day is late and the road is long; the day of repayment may never come. Surely this is not a matter of one contemptible man alone!

sentences.zh: 但才雖庸近，職居獻替，愚衷寸抱，敢不申陳。

translations.literal: Yet though my talent is mediocre and near, my office occupies offering and replacement; my foolish heart in an inch embrace—I dare not fail to state clearly.
translations.idiomatic: Yet though my ability is humble and my post only one of remonstrance, the thought in my heart cannot be held back, and I dare not fail to speak.

sentences.zh: 伏願聖慈少垂察覽，訪議槐棘，論其是非。

translations.literal: Humbly I wish Your sage compassion would slightly extend inspection; consult deliberation at locust and thorn and discuss right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg Your sage compassion to look into this, to consult the court at the locust-and-thorn gate, and judge right from wrong.

sentences.zh: 使秋霜春露，施之有在；

translations.literal: Let autumn frost and spring dew have a place to be applied;
translations.idiomatic: Let autumn frost and spring dew—the rites owed to the dead and the living—be rightly observed;

sentences.zh: 相鼠攸刺，遄死有歸。

translations.literal: The Ode of the Rat that one pricks—swift death has its destination.
translations.idiomatic: let the scorn of "Look at the Rat" strike home, and let swift death find its proper end.

sentences.zh: 無令申伋受笑於苟存，曾閔淪名於盛世。

translations.literal: Do not let Shen Ji be laughed at for clinging to life, nor Zeng Min lose his name in a sage era.
translations.idiomatic: Do not let Shen Ji become a laughingstock for clinging to life, nor Zeng Min lose his good name in an age of sage rule.

sentences.zh: 正德既至京師，朝廷待之尤薄。

translations.literal: Once Zhengde had arrived at the capital, the court treated him especially coldly.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhengde reached the capital, the court treated him with unusual coldness.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，還叛。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he returned and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: After a little more than a year, he went back and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 五年，蕭衍遣其將裴邃、虞鴻等率眾寇揚州，詔寶夤為使持節、散騎常侍、車騎大將軍、都督徐州東道諸軍事，率諸將討之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Xiao Yan sent his generals Pei Sui, Yu Hong, and others to lead troops raiding Yangzhou; an edict appointed Baoyin as Envoy Holding the Staff, Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Commander of all military affairs of the Eastern Route of Xuzhou, to lead the generals in suppressing them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Xiao Yan sent his generals Pei Sui, Yu Hong, and others to invade Yangzhou with an army. An edict made Baoyin Envoy Holding the Staff, Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Commander of all military affairs on the Eastern Route of Xuzhou, charging him to lead the generals against them.

sentences.zh: 既而揚州刺史長孫稚大破邃軍，斬鴻，賊遂奔退。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Yangzhou Inspector Changsun Zhi greatly defeated Sui's army, beheaded Hong, and the bandits then fled in retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Yangzhou Inspector Changsun Zhi routed Pei Sui's army, killed Yu Hong, and the enemy fled.

sentences.zh: 初，秦州城人薛珍、劉慶、杜遷等反，執刺史李彥，推莫折大提為首，自稱秦王。

translations.literal: Initially, the men of Qinzhou city—Xue Zhen, Liu Qing, Du Qian, and others—rebelled, seized Inspector Li Yan, and made Moqi Dati their leader, proclaiming himself King of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the townspeople of Qinzhou—Xue Zhen, Liu Qing, Du Qian, and others—rose in revolt, seized Inspector Li Yan, and set up Moqi Dati as their leader, who proclaimed himself King of Qin.

sentences.zh: 大提尋死，其第四子念生竊號天子，改年曰天建，置立官僚，以息阿胡為太子，其兄阿倪為西河王，弟天生為高陽王，伯珍為東郡王，安保為平陽王。

translations.literal: Dati soon died; his fourth son Niansheng usurped the title Son of Heaven, changed the era name to Tianjian, established officials, made Xi Ahu Crown Prince, his elder brother Ani King of Xihe, his younger brother Tiansheng King of Gaoyang, Bozhen King of Dongjun, and Anbao King of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Dati soon died. His fourth son Niansheng seized the title of Son of Heaven, changed the era name to Tianjian, established a full bureaucracy, made Xi Ahu crown prince, his elder brother Ani King of Xihe, his younger brother Tiansheng King of Gaoyang, Bozhen King of Dongjun, and Anbao King of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 遣天生率眾出隴東，攻沒汧城，仍陷岐州，執元志、裴芬之等，遂寇雍州，屯於黑水。

translations.literal: He sent Tiansheng to lead troops out through eastern Long, attacked and took Qian city, then captured Qizhou, seized Yuan Zhi, Pei Fenzhi, and others, then raided Yongzhou and encamped at Heishui.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Tiansheng to lead an army east out of Long, stormed and took Qian city, then seized Qizhou, captured Yuan Zhi, Pei Fenzhi, and others, and pressed on against Yongzhou, encamping at Heishui.

sentences.zh: 朝廷甚憂之，乃除寶夤開府、西道行臺，率所部東行將統，為大都督西征。

translations.literal: The court was greatly worried; it then appointed Baoyin as Opener of a Headquarters and Western Route Executive, leading his command eastward as commanding general, Grand Commander of the Western Expedition.
translations.idiomatic: The court was deeply alarmed and appointed Baoyin Opener of a Headquarters and head of the Western Route Executive, putting him in command of his forces marching east as Grand Commander of the Western Expedition.

sentences.zh: 肅宗幸明堂，因以餞之。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong visited the Bright Hall and there saw him off.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong visited the Bright Hall and there saw him off.

sentences.zh: 寶夤與大都督崔延伯擊天生，大破之，斬獲十餘萬。

translations.literal: Baoyin and Grand Commander Cui Yanbo struck Tiansheng and routed him, killing and capturing more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin and the Grand Commander Cui Yanbo attacked Tiansheng and crushed him, killing and capturing more than a hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 追奔至于小隴，軍人採掠，遂致稽留，不速追討，隴路復塞。

translations.literal: Pursuing the fugitives as far as Xiao Long, the soldiers plundered for provisions, thus causing delay; they did not pursue quickly, and the Long routes were blocked again.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit carried as far as Xiao Long, but the troops turned to looting, which slowed them down; failing to press the pursuit, the routes through Long were blocked once more.

sentences.zh: 仍進討高平賊帥万俟醜奴於安定，更有負捷。

translations.literal: They then advanced to attack the Gaoping bandit chief Wanqi Chunu at Anding and won further victories.
translations.idiomatic: They then moved against the Gaoping bandit chief Wanqi Chunu at Anding and won further victories.

sentences.zh: 時有天水人呂伯度兄弟，始共念生同逆，後與兄眾保於顯親，聚眾討念生，戰敗，降於胡琛。

translations.literal: At the time the Tianshui men Lü Bodu and his brothers at first joined Niansheng in rebellion; later, with their elder brother Zhong, they fortified themselves at Xianqin, gathered troops to attack Niansheng, were defeated, and surrendered to Hu Chen.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Tianshui brothers Lü Bodu and his kin had first rebelled alongside Niansheng, then withdrew with their elder brother Zhong to hold Xianqin, rallied men against Niansheng, were defeated, and surrendered to Hu Chen.

sentences.zh: 琛以伯度為大都督、秦王，資其士馬，還征秦州，大敗念生將杜粲於成紀，又破其金城王莫折普賢於水洛城，[8]遂至顯親。

translations.literal: Chen made Bodu Grand Commander and King of Qin, supplied him with troops and horses, and sent him back to campaign in Qinzhou; he greatly defeated Niansheng's general Du Can at Chenji, then broke his King of Jincheng Moqi Puxian at Shuilo city, [8] and advanced to Xianqin.
translations.idiomatic: Chen made Bodu Grand Commander and King of Qin, supplied him with troops and horses, and sent him back against Qinzhou. He routed Niansheng's general Du Can at Chenji, then defeated his King of Jincheng, Moqi Puxian, at Shuilo city, [8] and advanced as far as Xianqin.

sentences.zh: 念生率眾，身自拒戰，又大奔敗。

translations.literal: Niansheng led his troops and personally resisted in battle, and again suffered great rout.
translations.idiomatic: Niansheng led his army out to resist in person and was routed once again.

sentences.zh: 伯度乃背胡琛，襲琛將劉拔，破走之，遣其兄子忻和率騎東引國軍。

translations.literal: Bodu then turned against Hu Chen, attacked Chen's general Liu Ba, routed and drove him off, and sent his nephew Xinhe to lead cavalry east to guide the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: Bodu then turned on Hu Chen, attacked Chen's general Liu Ba and drove him off, and sent his nephew Xinhe east with cavalry to guide the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 念生事迫，乃詐降於寶夤。

translations.literal: Niansheng, pressed by circumstances, then feigned surrender to Baoyin.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed, Niansheng pretended to surrender to Baoyin.

sentences.zh: 朝廷喜伯度立義之功，授撫軍將軍、涇州刺史、平秦郡開國公，食邑三千戶。

translations.literal: The court rejoiced at Bodu's merit in establishing righteousness and appointed him General Who Pacifies the Army, Inspector of Jingzhou, Duke of Pingqian Commandery with a fief, with a fief of three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: The court delighted in Bodu's loyal service and made him General Who Pacifies the Army, Inspector of Jingzhou, and Duke of Pingqian Commandery with a fief of three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 而大都督元脩義、高聿，停軍隴口，久不西進。

translations.literal: But Grand Commanders Yuan Xiuyi and Gao Yu halted their armies at Longkou and for a long time did not advance west.
translations.idiomatic: But the Grand Commanders Yuan Xiuyi and Gao Yu halted at Longkou and for a long time failed to advance west.

sentences.zh: 念生復反，伯度終為醜奴所殺。

translations.literal: Niansheng rebelled again, and Bodu was finally killed by Chunu.
translations.idiomatic: Niansheng rebelled again, and Bodu was ultimately killed by Chunu.

sentences.zh: 故賊勢更甚，寶夤不能制。

translations.literal: Therefore the bandits' power grew still greater, and Baoyin could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels' power therefore grew still worse, and Baoyin could not bring them under control.

sentences.zh: 孝昌二年四月，除寶夤侍中、驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、假大將軍、尚書令，給後部鼓吹，增封千戶。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Xiaochang, Baoyin was appointed Palace Attendant, General of Swift Cavalry, Merit Equal to the Three Excellencies, Acting Great General, Minister Director of the Left, granted rear guard music, with an added fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year of Xiaochang, Baoyin was made Palace Attendant, General of Swift Cavalry, Merit Equal to the Three Excellencies, Acting Great General, and Minister Director of the Left, granted imperial music for his guard, and given an additional fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 寶夤初自黑水，終至平涼，與賊相對，數年攻擊，賊亦憚之，關中保全，寶夤之力矣。

translations.literal: From the time Baoyin first faced them at Heishui until he reached Pingliang, standing opposite the bandits for years of attack, the bandits also feared him; Guanzhong was preserved—it was Baoyin's doing.
translations.idiomatic: From his first stand at Heishui to his long campaign as far as Pingliang, he faced the rebels year after year; they feared him too, and Guanzhong was preserved—this was Baoyin's achievement.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，除司空公。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, he was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year he was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 出師既久，兵將疲弊，是月大敗，還雍州。

translations.literal: The campaign having lasted long, troops and generals were worn and exhausted; that month he suffered great defeat and returned to Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His campaign had dragged on too long; troops and commanders were worn out. That month he suffered a crushing defeat and withdrew to Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 仍停長安，收聚離散。

translations.literal: He then halted at Chang'an and gathered the scattered.
translations.idiomatic: He halted at Chang'an and gathered his scattered forces.

sentences.zh: 有司處寶夤死罪，詔恕為民。

translations.literal: The responsible offices sentenced Baoyin to death; an edict pardoned him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: The judicial offices sentenced Baoyin to death, but an edict pardoned him and reduced him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 四月，除使持節、都督雍涇岐南豳四州諸軍事、征西將軍、雍州刺史、假車騎大將軍、開府、西討大都督，自關以西，皆受節度。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, he was appointed Envoy Holding the Staff, Commander of all military affairs of the four provinces Yong, Jing, Qi, Southern Bin, General Who Campaigns West, Inspector of Yongzhou, Acting General of Chariots and Cavalry, Opener of a Headquarters, Grand Commander of the Western Punitive Campaign; from the Pass westward, all received his command.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he was reappointed Envoy Holding the Staff, Commander of all military affairs in Yong, Jing, Qi, and Southern Bin, General Who Campaigns West, Inspector of Yongzhou, Acting General of Chariots and Cavalry, Opener of a Headquarters, and Grand Commander of the Western Punitive Campaign, with all forces west of the Pass under his command.

sentences.zh: 九年，念生為其常山王杜粲所殺，合門皆盡。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Niansheng was killed by his King of Changshan Du Can, and the whole household was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Niansheng was killed by his King of Changshan, Du Can, and his entire household was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 粲據州請降於寶夤。

translations.literal: Can held the province and requested surrender to Baoyin.
translations.idiomatic: Du Can held the province and offered surrender to Baoyin.

sentences.zh: 十月，除散騎常侍、車騎將軍、尚書令，復其舊封。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Minister Director of the Left, and his former fief was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Minister Director of the Left, and his old fief was restored.

sentences.zh: 是時，山東、關西，寇賊充斥，王師屢北，人情沮喪。

translations.literal: At this time Shandong and Guanxi were filled with bandits and raiders; the imperial army repeatedly suffered northern defeats; men's hearts were dispirited.
translations.idiomatic: At that time bandits filled the eastern provinces and the west; the imperial army suffered defeat after defeat, and morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 寶夤自以出軍累年，糜費尤廣，一旦覆敗，慮見猜責，內不自安。

translations.literal: Baoyin, considering that he had campaigned for many years with especially broad expense, and had suddenly suffered total defeat, feared he would be suspected and blamed and was not at ease within.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin knew he had campaigned for years at enormous cost and had now suffered sudden ruin; he feared suspicion and blame and could not rest easy.

sentences.zh: 朝廷頗亦疑阻，乃遣御史中尉酈道元為關中大使。

translations.literal: The court also grew somewhat suspicious and obstructive, and sent Supervising Censor Li Daoyuan as ambassador to Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The court too grew suspicious, and sent the Supervising Censor Li Daoyuan to Guanzhong as imperial envoy.

sentences.zh: 寶夤謂密欲取己，彌以憂懼。

translations.literal: Baoyin thought they secretly wished to seize him and grew all the more anxious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin took this to mean they meant secretly to seize him, and his fear only grew.

sentences.zh: 而長安輕薄之徒，因相說動。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the frivolous crowd of Chang'an incited one another among themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the idle and reckless men of Chang'an egged one another on.

sentences.zh: 道元行達陰盤驛，寶夤密遣其將郭子恢等攻而殺之，詐收道元尸，表言白賊所害。

translations.literal: When Daoyuan's journey reached Yinpan Post, Baoyin secretly sent his generals Guo Zihui and others to attack and kill him, falsely seized Daoyuan's corpse, and memorialized that White Bandits had killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Daoyuan reached Yinpan Post on his journey, Baoyin secretly sent his generals Guo Zihui and others to attack and kill him, seized his body under false pretenses, and memorialized that he had been killed by White Bandits.

sentences.zh: 又殺都督、南平王仲冏。

translations.literal: He also killed the Commander, the Prince of Nanping, Zhongjiong.
translations.idiomatic: He also killed the Commander, Prince of Nanping, Zhongjiong.

sentences.zh: 是月，遂反，僭舉大號，赦其部內，稱隆緒元年，立百官。

translations.literal: That month he then rebelled, usurped a great title, proclaimed amnesty within his command, took the era name Longxu year one, and established officials.
translations.idiomatic: That same month he rebelled, proclaimed himself emperor, granted amnesty within his domains, adopted the era name Longxu, year one, and established a full bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 乃遣郭子恢東寇潼關，行臺張始榮圍華州刺史崔襲。

translations.literal: He then sent Guo Zihui east to raid Tong Pass, while Executive Zhang Shirong besieged Huazhou Inspector Cui Xi.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Guo Zihui east against Tong Pass, while the Executive Zhang Shirong besieged Cui Xi, the Inspector of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 詔尚書僕射行臺長孫稚討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Minister Secretary Executive Changsun Zhi to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Minister Secretary and Executive Changsun Zhi to put him down.

sentences.zh: 時北地人毛鴻賓與其兄遐糾率鄉義，將討寶夤。

translations.literal: At the time the Beidi man Mao Hongbin and his elder brother Xia rallied township righteousness and were about to attack Baoyin.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Mao Hongbin of Beidi and his elder brother Xia rallied local loyalists to move against Baoyin.

sentences.zh: 寶夤遣其大將軍盧祖遷等擊遐，為遐所殺。

translations.literal: Baoyin sent his Great General Lu Zuqian and others to strike Xia, and they were killed by Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin sent his Great General Lu Zuqian and others against Xia, and they were killed by him.

sentences.zh: 又遣其將侯終德往攻遐。

translations.literal: He also sent his general Hou Zhongde to go attack Xia.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent his general Hou Zhongde to attack Xia.

sentences.zh: 會子恢為官軍所敗，長孫稚又遣子子彥破始榮於華州，終德因此勢挫，還圖寶夤。

translations.literal: Just then Zihui was defeated by the imperial army; Changsun Zhi also sent his son Ziyan to defeat Shirong at Huazhou; Zhongde's momentum was thus broken, and he turned to plot against Baoyin.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Zihui was defeated by the imperial army, and Changsun Zhi sent his son Ziyan to rout Shirong at Huazhou. Zhongde's force was broken, and he turned to plot against Baoyin.

sentences.zh: 軍至白門，寶夤始覺，與終德交戰，戰敗，攜公主及其少子與部下百餘騎，從後門出走，渡渭橋，投於寧夷巴張宕昌、劉興周舍。

translations.literal: When the army reached White Gate, Baoyin finally realized it; he fought Zhongde in battle, was defeated, took the princess and his youngest son with more than a hundred followers on horseback, fled out the rear gate, crossed Wei Bridge, and fled to the houses of the Ningyi Ba, Zhang Danchang and Liu Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached White Gate, Baoyin finally realized what was happening. He fought Zhongde and was defeated, then fled with the princess, his youngest son, and a little over a hundred horsemen through the rear gate, crossed Wei Bridge, and took refuge with the Ningyi Ba chiefs Zhang Danchang and Liu Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋奔醜奴，醜奴以寶夤為太傅。

translations.literal: Soon he fled to Chunu, and Chunu made Baoyin Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He soon fled to Chunu, who made him Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 永安三年，都督尒朱天光遣賀拔岳等破醜奴於安定，追擒醜奴、寶夤，並送京師。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yong'an, Commander Erzhu Tianguang sent Heba Yue and others to defeat Chunu at Anding, pursued and captured Chunu and Baoyin, and sent them together to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yong'an the Commander Erzhu Tianguang sent Heba Yue and others to defeat Chunu at Anding, pursued and captured both Chunu and Baoyin, and sent them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 詔置閶闔門外都街之中，京師士女，聚共觀視，凡經三日。

translations.literal: An edict ordered them placed in the capital street outside Changhe Gate; the men and women of the capital gathered to watch together—for three days in all.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had them placed in the main street outside Changhe Gate, and for three days the men and women of the capital gathered to watch.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書李神儁、黃門侍郎高道穆並與寶夤素舊，二人相與左右，言於莊帝，云「其逆亦事在前朝」，冀得赦免。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Li Shenjun and Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Gao Daomu were both old friends of Baoyin; the two supported him on either side, speaking to Emperor Zhuang, saying, "His rebellion was also a matter of the previous reign," hoping to obtain pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenjun, Minister of Personnel, and Gao Daomu, Vice Director of the Yellow Gate, were both old friends of Baoyin. The two sided with him and told Emperor Zhuang, "His rebellion belongs to the affairs of the previous reign as well," hoping he might be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 會應詔王道習時自外至，莊帝問道習在外所聞。

translations.literal: Just then Wang Daoxi, responding to an edict, arrived from outside; Emperor Zhuang asked Daoxi what he had heard outside.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Wang Daoxi, summoned by edict, arrived from outside the palace, and Emperor Zhuang asked what he had heard beyond the gates.

sentences.zh: 道習曰：「唯聞陛下欲不殺蕭寶夤。

translations.literal: Daoxi said: "I have only heard that Your Majesty wishes not to execute Xiao Baoyin.
translations.idiomatic: Daoxi said, "I have only heard that Your Majesty does not intend to execute Xiao Baoyin.

sentences.zh: 」帝問其故。

translations.literal: " The Emperor asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor asked why.

sentences.zh: 道習曰：「人云：李尚書、高黃門與寶夤周款，並居得言之地，必能全之。

translations.literal: Daoxi said: "People say: Minister Li and Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Gao are on intimate terms with Baoyin; both hold positions where they can speak freely, and will surely be able to save him.
translations.idiomatic: Daoxi said, "People say Minister Li and Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Gao are on close terms with Baoyin. Both hold posts where they can speak freely, and will surely save him.

sentences.zh: 」道習因曰：「若謂寶夤逆在前朝，便將恕之。

translations.literal: " Daoxi then said: "If one holds that Baoyin's rebellion belongs to the previous reign, then one will pardon him.
translations.idiomatic: Daoxi went on, "If Baoyin's rebellion is treated as a matter of the previous reign, then he will be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 寶夤敗於長安，走為醜奴太傅，豈非陛下御曆之日？

translations.literal: Baoyin was defeated at Chang'an and fled to become Chunu's Grand Tutor—was that not during the days of Your Majesty's accession to the throne?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Baoyin was defeated at Chang'an and fled to become Chunu's Grand Tutor—was that not after Your Majesty had already ascended the throne?

sentences.zh: 賊臣不翦，法欲安施？

translations.literal: If a treacherous minister is not cut down, how is the law to be applied?
translations.idiomatic: If a traitorous minister is not cut down, how can the law be upheld?

sentences.zh: 」帝然其言，乃於太僕駞牛署賜死。

translations.literal: " The Emperor approved his words and thereupon granted death by poison at the Chief of Palace Transportation's Camel Office.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor agreed and ordered Baoyin granted death by poison at the Chief of Palace Transportation's Camel Office.

sentences.zh: 寶夤之將死，神儁攜酒就之以敍舊故，因對之下泣。

translations.literal: As Baoyin was about to die, Shenjun brought wine and went to him to renew old friendship, and wept facing him.
translations.idiomatic: As Baoyin was about to die, Shenjun brought wine to renew their old friendship and wept before him.

sentences.zh: 而寶夤夷然自持，了不憂懼，唯稱「推天委命，恨不終臣節」而已。

translations.literal: But Baoyin remained calm and self-possessed, utterly without worry or fear, saying only, "I defer to Heaven and accept fate; I regret only that I could not finish my service as a minister."
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin, however, remained calm and composed, without fear or distress, saying only, "I defer to Heaven and accept my fate. I regret only that I could not remain a loyal minister to the end."

sentences.zh: 公主攜男女就寶夤訣別，慟哭極哀。

translations.literal: The princess brought her sons and daughters to Baoyin for a final parting, weeping with utmost grief.
translations.idiomatic: The princess brought her children to Baoyin for a final farewell, weeping in deepest grief.

sentences.zh: 寶夤死，色貌不改。

translations.literal: When Baoyin died, his complexion did not change.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin died, his face did not change.

sentences.zh: 寶夤有三子，皆公主所生，而並凡劣。

translations.literal: Baoyin had three sons, all born to the princess, and all were mediocre and inferior.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin had three sons, all born to the princess, and all were undistinguished.

sentences.zh: 長子烈，復尚肅宗妹建德公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: The eldest son Lie again married Emperor Suzong's younger sister, Princess Jian'de, and was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son, Lie, again married Emperor Suzong's younger sister, Princess Jian'de, and was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law.

sentences.zh: 寶夤反，伏法。

translations.literal: When Baoyin rebelled, he was executed by law.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin rebelled, Lie was executed by law.

sentences.zh: 次子權，與少子凱射戲，凱矢激中之而死。

translations.literal: The second son Quan and the youngest son Kai were playing at archery; Kai's arrow ricocheted and struck Quan, killing him.
translations.idiomatic: The second son Quan and the youngest son Kai were shooting at targets for sport when Kai's arrow ricocheted and struck Quan, killing him.

sentences.zh: 凱仕至司徒左長史。

translations.literal: Kai rose in office to Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Kai rose to the post of Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 凱妻，長孫稚女也，輕薄無禮，公主數加罪責。

translations.literal: Kai's wife was the daughter of Changsun Zhi; she was frivolous and without propriety, and the princess repeatedly censured and punished her.
translations.idiomatic: Kai's wife was Changsun Zhi's daughter. She was frivolous and disrespectful, and the princess repeatedly rebuked and punished her.

sentences.zh: 凱竊銜恨，妻復惑說之。

translations.literal: Kai secretly harbored resentment, and his wife further incited him.
translations.idiomatic: Kai secretly nursed resentment, and his wife further goaded him on.

sentences.zh: 天平中，凱遂遣奴害公主。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era, Kai then sent a slave to kill the princess.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianping era, Kai sent a slave to kill the princess.

sentences.zh: 乃轘凱於東巿，妻梟首。

translations.literal: Kai was then torn apart at the Eastern Market, and his wife's head was exposed on a pole.
translations.idiomatic: Kai was then torn apart at the Eastern Market, and his wife's head was displayed on a pole.

sentences.zh: 家遂殄滅。

translations.literal: The family was thus exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: The family was thus wiped out.

sentences.zh: 寶夤兄寶卷子贊，字德文，本名綜，入國，寶夤改焉。

translations.literal: Baoyin's elder brother Baojuan's son Zan, styled Dewen, originally named Zong; upon entering the state, Baoyin changed it.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin's elder brother Baojuan had a son Zan, styled Dewen, originally named Zong; when he entered Wei, Baoyin changed his name.

sentences.zh: 初，蕭衍滅寶卷，寶卷宮人吳氏始孕，匿而不言，衍仍納之，生贊，以為己子，封豫章王。

translations.literal: Initially, when Xiao Yan destroyed Baojuan, the palace woman of Baojuan, Lady Wu, had just conceived; she concealed it and did not speak of it. Yan still took her in, and she bore Zan, whom he treated as his own son and enfeoffed as Prince of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Yan overthrew Baojuan, Baojuan's palace woman Lady Wu had just conceived. She hid the pregnancy and said nothing, yet Yan still took her in. She bore Zan, whom Yan treated as his own son and enfeoffed as Prince of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 及長，學涉，有才思。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he was broadly learned and had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up, he was well read and gifted with literary talent.

sentences.zh: 其母告之以實，贊晝則談謔如常，夜則銜悲泣涕，結客待士，恒有來奔之志。

translations.literal: His mother told him the truth; by day Zan joked and bantered as usual, but at night he grieved and wept, gathering guests and treating scholars, always with the will to flee north.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother told him the truth, Zan joked and chatted by day as always, but at night he grieved and wept. He gathered followers and treated men of talent, always longing to flee north.

sentences.zh: 為衍諸子深所猜疾，而衍甚愛寵之。

translations.literal: Yan's sons deeply suspected and resented him, yet Yan greatly loved and favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's sons deeply distrusted and resented him, yet Yan himself greatly loved and favored him.

sentences.zh: 有濟陰芮文寵、安定梁話，贊曲加禮接，乃割血自誓，布以腹心。

translations.literal: There were Rui Wenchong of Jiyin and Liang Hua of Anding; Zan treated them with special courtesy, then cut his flesh and swore an oath, opening his innermost heart to them.
translations.idiomatic: There were Rui Wenchong of Jiyin and Liang Hua of Anding. Zan treated them with especial courtesy, cut his flesh to swear an oath, and laid bare his innermost heart.

sentences.zh: 寵、話等既感其情義，敬相然諾。

translations.literal: Wenchong, Hua, and the others, moved by his affection and righteousness, respectfully pledged themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his loyalty and affection, Wenchong, Hua, and the others pledged themselves to him in earnest.

sentences.zh: 值元法僧以彭城叛入蕭衍，衍命贊為南兗、徐二州刺史、都督江北諸軍事，鎮彭城。

translations.literal: Just then Yuan Faseng rebelled at Pengcheng and entered Xiao Yan's service; Yan appointed Zan Inspector of the two provinces Southern Yan and Xu, Commander of all military affairs north of the Yangtze, stationed at Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Faseng rebelled at Pengcheng and went over to Xiao Yan, Yan made Zan Inspector of Southern Yan and Xu, Commander of all military affairs north of the Yangtze, with his headquarters at Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 於時，肅宗遣安豐王延明、臨淮王彧討之，贊便遣使密告誠款，與寵、話夜出，步投彧軍。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Suzong sent the Prince of Anfeng Yanming and the Prince of Linhuai Yu to suppress him. Zan then sent an envoy to secretly declare his sincere allegiance, and with Wenchong and Hua went out by night on foot and joined Yu's army.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong then sent the Prince of Anfeng, Yanming, and the Prince of Linhuai, Yu, against him. Zan secretly sent envoys to declare his loyalty, then slipped out by night with Wenchong and Hua on foot and joined Yu's army.

sentences.zh: 孝昌元年秋，屆于洛陽，陛見之後，就館舉哀，追服三載。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the first year of Xiaochang, he arrived at Luoyang; after audience with the throne, he went to his lodging and performed mourning, observing three years of mourning retroactively.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the first year of Xiaochang he reached Luoyang. After audience with the throne he went to his lodging and mourned, observing three years of mourning retroactively.

sentences.zh: 寶夤于時在關西，遣使觀察，聞其形貌，斂眉悲感。

translations.literal: Baoyin was then in Guanxi and sent an envoy to observe him; hearing of his appearance, he knit his brows in sorrowful feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin was then in the west and sent an envoy to observe him. When he heard of Zan's appearance, he knit his brows in sorrow.

sentences.zh: 朝廷賞賜豐渥，禮遇隆厚，授司空，封高平郡開國公、丹陽王，食邑七千戶。

translations.literal: The court rewarded him richly and treated him with lofty honor, appointing him Minister of Works, enfeoffing him as Duke of Gaoping Commandery with a state and Prince of Danyang, with a fief of seven thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: The court rewarded him lavishly and treated him with great honor, appointing him Minister of Works, enfeoffing him as Duke of Gaoping Commandery and Prince of Danyang, with a fief of seven thousand households.

sentences.zh: 及寶夤反，贊惶怖，欲奔白鹿山，至河橋，為北中所執。

translations.literal: When Baoyin rebelled, Zan was terrified and wished to flee to Bailu Mountain; reaching He Bridge, he was seized by the northern garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin rebelled, Zan was terrified and tried to flee to Bailu Mountain. At He Bridge he was seized by the northern garrison.

sentences.zh: 朝議明其不相干預，仍蒙慰勉。

translations.literal: Court deliberation made clear that he had not been involved, and he still received consolation and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: The court found that he had had no part in it and still treated him with reassurance and encouragement.

sentences.zh: 建義初，隨尒朱榮赴晉陽，莊帝徵贊還洛。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi, he followed Erzhu Rong to Jinyang; Emperor Zhuang summoned Zan back to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianyi he followed Erzhu Rong to Jinyang, and Emperor Zhuang summoned Zan back to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 轉司徒，遷太尉，尚帝姊壽陽長公主。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Education, promoted to Grand Commandant, and married the Emperor's elder sister, Princess of Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Minister of Education, then Grand Commandant, and married the Emperor's elder sister, the Princess of Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 出為都督齊濟西兗三州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、齊州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Commander of all military affairs of the three provinces Qi, Western Ji, and Yan, General of Swift Cavalry, Merit Equal to the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Commander of all military affairs in Qi, Western Ji, and Yan, General of Swift Cavalry, Merit Equal to the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 寶夤見擒，贊拜表請寶夤命。

translations.literal: When Baoyin was captured, Zan submitted a memorial requesting Baoyin's life.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin was captured, Zan submitted a memorial begging for his life.

sentences.zh: 尒朱兆入洛，為城民趙洛周所逐。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, he was driven off by the townsman Zhao Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Zan was driven off by the townsman Zhao Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 公主被錄還京，尒朱世隆欲相陵逼，公主守操被害。

translations.literal: The princess was seized and sent back to the capital; Erzhu Shilong wished to force himself upon her, and the princess, guarding her virtue, was killed.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was seized and sent back to the capital. Erzhu Shilong tried to force himself upon her, and the princess, defending her virtue, was killed.

sentences.zh: 贊既棄州為沙門，潛詣長白山，未幾，趣白鹿山。

translations.literal: Zan, having abandoned his province, became a monk and secretly went to Mount Changbai; before long he made for Bailu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Zan abandoned his province and became a monk, secretly making for Mount Changbai; before long he set out for Bailu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 至陽平，遇病而卒，時年三十一。

translations.literal: Reaching Yangping, he fell ill and died, aged thirty-one.
translations.idiomatic: At Yangping he fell ill and died, aged thirty-one.

sentences.zh: 贊機辯，文義頗有可觀，而輕薄俶儻，猶見父之風尚。

translations.literal: Zan was quick and eloquent, and his literary compositions were quite worth viewing, yet he was frivolous and unrestrained—still showing his father's character and style.
translations.idiomatic: Zan was quick-witted and eloquent, and his writing was not without merit, yet he was frivolous and unrestrained—still showing his father's character.

sentences.zh: 普泰末，敕迎其喪至洛，遣黃門郎鹿悆護喪事，以王禮與公主合葬嵩山。

translations.literal: At the end of Putai, an edict ordered his coffin brought to Luoyang; Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Lu Yu was sent to oversee the funeral, and he was buried on Mount Song with princely rites together with the princess.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Putai an edict had his coffin brought to Luoyang. Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Lu Yu was sent to oversee the funeral, and Zan was buried on Mount Song with princely rites beside the princess.

sentences.zh: 至元象初，吳人盜其喪還江東，蕭衍猶以為子，祔葬蕭氏墓焉。

translations.literal: By the beginning of Yuanxiang, Wu men stole his coffin and returned it to Jiangdong; Xiao Yan still treated him as his son and buried him beside the Xiao clan tombs.
translations.idiomatic: By the beginning of Yuanxiang, men of Wu stole his coffin and took it back to Jiangdong. Xiao Yan still treated him as his son and buried him in the Xiao family tombs.

sentences.zh: 贊江南有子，在國無後。

translations.literal: Zan had a son in Jiangnan; in the northern state he left no descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Zan had a son in the south; in the north he left no descendants.

sentences.zh: 蕭正表，字公儀，蕭衍弟臨川王宣達子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Zhengbiao, styled Gongyi, was the son of Xiao Yan's younger brother, the Prince of Linchuan Xuanda.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zhengbiao, styled Gongyi, was the son of Xiao Yan's younger brother, the Prince of Linchuan, Xuanda.

sentences.zh: 正表長七尺九寸，眉目疏朗。

translations.literal: Zhengbiao was seven feet nine inches tall, with clear brows and eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengbiao stood seven feet nine inches tall, with clear, handsome features.

sentences.zh: 雖質貌豐美，而性理短闇。

translations.literal: Although his appearance was rich and beautiful, his nature and understanding were shallow and dim.
translations.idiomatic: Though handsome and well favored, his mind was shallow and dull.

sentences.zh: 衍以為封山縣開國侯，拜給事中，歷東宮洗馬、淮南晉安二郡太守。

translations.literal: Yan made him Marquis of Fengshan Commandery with a state, appointed him Palace Attendant, and he served successively as Palace Groom of the Eastern Palace and Governor of the two commanderies Huainan and Jin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yan made him Marquis of Fengshan Commandery, appointed him Palace Attendant, and he served as Palace Groom of the Eastern Palace and Governor of Huainan and Jin'an.

sentences.zh: 轉輕車將軍、北徐州刺史，鎮鍾離。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Light Chariots and Inspector of Northern Xuzhou, stationed at Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General of the Light Chariots and Inspector of Northern Xuzhou, with his headquarters at Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 初，衍未有子，以正表兄正德為子，既而封為西豐侯。

translations.literal: Initially, before Yan had a son, he took Zhengbiao's elder cousin Zhengde as his son; afterward he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xifeng.
translations.idiomatic: At first, before Yan had a son of his own, he adopted Zhengbiao's elder cousin Zhengde and later enfeoffed him as Marquis of Xifeng.

sentences.zh: 正德私懷忿憾。

translations.literal: Zhengde privately harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde secretly nursed resentment.

sentences.zh: 正光三年，背衍奔洛，朝廷以其人才庸劣，不加禮待。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengguang, he turned against Yan and fled to Luoyang; the court, considering his talent mediocre and inferior, did not treat him with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhengguang he turned against Yan and fled to Luoyang. The court, judging his talent mediocre, did not treat him with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 尋逃歸，衍不之罪。

translations.literal: Soon he escaped and returned; Yan did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: He soon escaped back south, and Yan did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 後封正德臨賀王。

translations.literal: Later Zhengde was enfeoffed as Prince of Linhe.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhengde was enfeoffed as Prince of Linhe.

sentences.zh: 衍末，復為散騎常侍、光祿大夫，知丹陽尹事。

translations.literal: Near the end of Yan's reign, he again served as Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and overseer of the office of Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Yan's reign he again served as Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and acting Governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 侯景之將濟江也，知正德有恨於衍，密與交通，許推為主。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing was about to cross the Yangtze, knowing that Zhengde bore a grudge against Yan, he secretly communicated with him and promised to set him up as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing was about to cross the Yangtze, knowing Zhengde resented Yan, he secretly contacted him and promised to make him ruler.

sentences.zh: 正德以船數十舫迎之。

translations.literal: Zhengde welcomed him with several dozen boats.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde welcomed him with several dozen boats.

sentences.zh: 景渡江，衍召正表入援。

translations.literal: When Jing crossed the river, Yan summoned Zhengbiao to come to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing crossed the river, Yan summoned Zhengbiao to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 正表率眾次廣陵，聞正德為侯景所推，仍託舫糧未集，磬桓不進。

translations.literal: Zhengbiao led his troops and halted at Guangling; hearing that Zhengde had been set up by Hou Jing, he still pleaded that boat provisions were not yet gathered and lingered without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengbiao led his troops and halted at Guangling. Learning that Hou Jing had set up Zhengde, he pleaded that boat supplies were not yet ready and lingered without advancing.

sentences.zh: 景尋以正表為南兗州刺史，封南郡王。
