translations.literal: Jing soon made Zhengbiao Inspector of Southern Yan Province and enfeoffed him as Prince of Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Jing soon made Zhengbiao Inspector of Southern Yan Province and enfeoffed him as Prince of Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 正表既受景署，遂於歐陽立柵，斷衍援軍。

translations.literal: Once Zhengbiao had accepted Jing's commission, he then built a palisade at Ouyang and cut off Yan's relief forces.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhengbiao accepted Jing's commission, he built a palisade at Ouyang and cut off Yan's relief forces.

sentences.zh: 又欲遣其妾兄龔子明進攻廣陵。

translations.literal: He also wished to send his concubine's elder brother Gong Ziming to attack Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: He also planned to send his concubine's elder brother, Gong Ziming, to attack Guangling.

sentences.zh: 衍南兗州刺史、南康王蕭會理遣前廣陵令劉瑗襲擊，破之。

translations.literal: Yan's Inspector of Southern Yan Province, the Prince of Nankang Xiao Huili, sent the former Magistrate of Guangling Liu Yuan to strike and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's Inspector of Southern Yan Province, the Prince of Nankang, Xiao Huili, sent the former Magistrate of Guangling, Liu Yuan, against him and routed him.

sentences.zh: 正表狼狽失據，乃率輕騎，走還鍾離。

translations.literal: Zhengbiao, in distress and without footing, then led light cavalry and fled back to Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengbiao, disgraced and left without footing, fled with light cavalry back to Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 武定七年正月，仍送子為質，據州內屬。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year of Wuding, he again sent his son as hostage and held the province in submission to the northern court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year of Wuding he again sent his son as hostage and submitted his province to the northern court.

sentences.zh: 徐州刺史高歸彥遣長史劉士榮馳赴之。

translations.literal: Xuzhou Inspector Gao Guiyan sent Chief Clerk Liu Shirong to ride posthaste to him.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuzhou Inspector Gao Guiyan sent Chief Clerk Liu Shirong to him at full speed.

sentences.zh: 事定，正表入朝，以勳封蘭陵郡開國公、吳郡王，食邑五千戶。

translations.literal: Once matters were settled, Zhengbiao entered court and, for his merit, was enfeoffed as Duke of Lanling Commandery with a state and Prince of Wu Commandery, with a fief of five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When matters were settled, Zhengbiao came to court and, for his service, was enfeoffed as Duke of Lanling Commandery and Prince of Wu Commandery, with a fief of five thousand households.

sentences.zh: 尋除侍中、車騎將軍、特進、太子太保、開府儀同三司，賞賚豐厚。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Palace Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Special Advance, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Merit Equal to the Three Excellencies, with rich rewards.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Palace Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Special Advance, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and Merit Equal to the Three Excellencies, with lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 其年冬薨，年四十二。

translations.literal: That winter he died, aged forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died that winter, aged forty-two.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、都督徐揚兗豫濟五州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、司空公、徐州刺史，開國公、王並如故。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted Palace Attendant, Commander of all military affairs of the five provinces Xu, Yang, Yan, Yu, and Ji, General of Swift Cavalry, Minister of Works, and Inspector of Xuzhou; his ducal state and princely title remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted Palace Attendant, Commander of all military affairs in Xu, Yang, Yan, Yu, and Ji, General of Swift Cavalry, Minister of Works, and Inspector of Xuzhou; his ducal and princely titles remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 諡曰昭烈。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Zhaolie.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Zhaolie, "Illustrious and Fierce."

sentences.zh: 子廣壽。

translations.literal: His son was Guangshou.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Guangshou.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：劉昶猜疑懼禍，蕭夤亡破之餘，並潛骸竄影，委命上國。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Liu Chang was suspicious and feared disaster; Xiao Baoyin, in the wreckage of ruin, both hid their bones and stole away their shadows, entrusting their lives to the northern state.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Liu Chang, suspicious and fearing disaster, and Xiao Baoyin, in the wreckage of defeat, both hid themselves and entrusted their lives to the northern court.

sentences.zh: 俱稱曉了，咸當任遇，雖有枕戈之志，終無鞭墓之誠。

translations.literal: Both were called clever and capable and both received appointment and favor; though they had the will to sleep with a spear at the head, in the end they had no true resolve to whip the grave.
translations.idiomatic: Both were called clever and capable and both received office and favor. Though they kept the will to sleep with a spear at the pillow, in the end they lacked the resolve to avenge the dead at the grave.

sentences.zh: 昶諸子尩疏，喪其家業。

translations.literal: Chang's sons were weak and deficient, and lost their family estate.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's sons were weak and undistinguished, and lost the family estate.

sentences.zh: 寶夤背恩忘義，梟鏡其心。

translations.literal: Baoyin betrayed grace and forgot righteousness; owl and mirror were his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin betrayed grace and forgot righteousness; his heart was that of an owl before a mirror.

sentences.zh: 此亦戎夷彯狡輕薄之常事也。

translations.literal: This too is the common affair of fierce, cunning, and frivolous barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: This too is the common way of fierce, cunning, and frivolous frontier men.

sentences.zh: 天重其罪，鬼覆其門，至於母子兄弟還相殲滅，抑是積惡之義云。

translations.literal: Heaven weighted his crimes; ghosts overturned his gate; as for mother, sons, and brothers destroying one another in turn, this is indeed the principle of accumulated evil.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven heaped guilt upon him; ghosts overturned his house. That mother, sons, and brothers in turn destroyed one another is the working out of accumulated evil.

sentences.zh: 蕭贊臨邊脫身，晚去讎賊，寵祿頓臻，顛沛旋至，信吉凶之相倚也。

translations.literal: Xiao Zan escaped at the frontier and left the enemy late; favor and salary came suddenly, and hardship followed at once—truly fortune and misfortune lean upon each other.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zan slipped away at the frontier and broke with the enemy only late; honors came in a rush, and ruin followed at once—truly fortune and misfortune depend on each other.

sentences.zh: 正表歸命，大享名族，亦以優哉。

translations.literal: Zhengbiao submitted to the northern court and greatly enjoyed noble rank—it too was a comfortable lot.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengbiao submitted to the northern court and enjoyed great honors—a comfortable lot indeed.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

sentences.zh: 遣典籤虞法生表求入朝 宋書卷七二、南史卷一四晉熙王昶傳、通鑑卷一三０

translations.literal: Sent dispatch clerk Yu Fasheng to submit a memorial requesting entry to court — Song Shu vol. 72, Nan Shi vol. 14 Biography of Jinxi Prince Liu Chang, Zizhi Tongjian vol. 130
translations.idiomatic: Sent dispatch clerk Yu Fasheng to submit a memorial requesting entry to court — Song Shu vol. 72, Nan Shi vol. 14 Biography of Jinxi Prince Liu Chang, Zizhi Tongjian vol. 130

sentences.zh: 〈四０七八頁〉

translations.literal: 〈Page 4078〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Page 4078〉

sentences.zh: 「虞」並作「蘧」，疑「虞」字訛。

translations.literal: Both read "Qu" for "Yu"; "Yu" is suspected to be corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Both read Qu instead of Yu; Yu is suspected to be a corrupt reading.

sentences.zh: 為兄弟之戒 北史卷二九劉昶傳「戒」作「式」。

translations.literal: As a warning to brothers — in Beishi vol. 29 Biography of Liu Chang, "warning" is written as "pattern."
translations.idiomatic: As a warning to brothers — in Beishi vol. 29, Biography of Liu Chang, warning is written as pattern.

sentences.zh: 疑「戒」字訛。

translations.literal: "Warning" is suspected to be corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Warning is suspected to be a corrupt reading.

sentences.zh: 乃請喪居斬衰之服 北史卷二九蕭寶夤傳「居」作「君」，指蕭寶卷，疑「居」字訛。

translations.literal: Then requested mourning garments of the severest grade — in Beishi vol. 29 Biography of Xiao Baoyin, "dwelling" is written as "lord," referring to Xiao Baojuan; "dwelling" is suspected to be corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Then requested mourning garments of the severest grade — in Beishi vol. 29, Biography of Xiao Baoyin, dwelling is written as lord, referring to Xiao Baojuan; dwelling is suspected to be a corrupt reading.

sentences.zh: 微子陳韓亦曷以過也 李慈銘云：「『陳韓』本作『陳完』，以南宋避欽宗嫌名，於『陳』下注一『諱』字，遂誤為『韓』。

translations.literal: How could Weizi and Chen Han have gone too far? Li Ciming says: "Chen Han" was originally "Chen Wan"; in the Southern Song, to avoid the taboo name of Emperor Qinzong, a note "taboo" was placed below Chen, and it was mistakenly read as Han.
translations.idiomatic: How could Weizi and Chen Han have gone too far? Li Ciming says: Chen Han was originally Chen Wan; in the Southern Song, to avoid the taboo name of Emperor Qinzong, a note reading taboo was placed below Chen, and it was mistakenly read as Han.

sentences.zh: 」按陳公子完奔齊，見左傳莊二十二年，李說疑是。

translations.literal: " According to the Zuo Zhuan, year 22 of Duke Zhuang, the son of the Chen lord Wan fled to Qi; Li's explanation is probably correct.
translations.idiomatic: " According to the Zuo Zhuan, Duke Zhuang year 22, the son of the lord of Chen, Wan, fled to Qi; Li's explanation is probably correct.

sentences.zh: 但卷七九成淹傳亦有「欲追縱陳韓」語，似指陳平、韓信背楚歸漢，今不改。

translations.literal: But vol. 79 Biography of Cheng Yan also has the phrase "wishing to pursue Chen Han," which seems to refer to Chen Ping and Han Xin turning from Chu to Han; the text is not changed here.
translations.idiomatic: But vol. 79, Biography of Cheng Yan, also has the phrase wishing to pursue Chen Han, which seems to refer to Chen Ping and Han Xin turning from Chu to Han; the text is not changed here.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍江州刺史陳伯之與其長史褚冑等自壽春歸降 北史卷二九百衲本同，汲本、殿本作「胃」。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's Inspector of Jiang Province Chen Bozhi and his Chief Clerk Chu Zhou and others surrendered from Shouyang — Beishi vol. 29, Baona edition agrees; Jiben and Dianben read "stomach."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan's Inspector of Jiang Province Chen Bozhi and his Chief Clerk Chu Zhou and others surrendered from Shouyang — Beishi vol. 29, Baona edition agrees; Jiben and Dianben read stomach.

sentences.zh: 按梁書卷二０陳伯之傳、通鑑卷一四五

translations.literal: According to Liang Shu vol. 20 Biography of Chen Bozhi, Zizhi Tongjian vol. 145
translations.idiomatic: According to Liang Shu vol. 20, Biography of Chen Bozhi, and Zizhi Tongjian vol. 145

sentences.zh: 〈四五二一頁〉

translations.literal: 〈Page 4521〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Page 4521〉

sentences.zh: 作「褚緭」，考異云：「魏書蕭寶夤傳作『褚胃』，今從梁書。

translations.literal: It reads "Chu Wei"; Kaoyi says: "The Wei Shu Biography of Xiao Baoyin reads Chu stomach; now following Liang Shu.
translations.idiomatic: It reads Chu Wei; Kaoyi says: The Wei Shu Biography of Xiao Baoyin reads Chu stomach; the text now follows Liang Shu.

sentences.zh: 」則司馬光所見魏書作亦「胃」。

translations.literal: " Then the Wei Shu text seen by Sima Guang also read "stomach."
translations.idiomatic: " The Wei Shu text seen by Sima Guang also read stomach.

sentences.zh: 「緭」「胃」同音，「冑」當是「胃」之訛。

translations.literal: "Wei" and "stomach" are homophones; "Zhou" is probably a corrupt form of "stomach."
translations.idiomatic: Wei and stomach are homophones; Zhou is probably a corrupt form of stomach.

sentences.zh: 除使持節都督東揚南徐兗三州諸軍事鎮東將軍東揚州刺史 諸本「揚州」上無「東」字，北史卷二九有。

translations.literal: Appointed Envoy Holding the Staff, Commander of all military affairs of the three provinces Eastern Yang, Southern Xu, and Yan, General Who Pacifies the East, and Inspector of Eastern Yang Province — in all editions "Eastern" is lacking before "Yang Province"; Beishi vol. 29 has it.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed Envoy Holding the Staff, Commander of all military affairs in Eastern Yang, Southern Xu, and Yan, General Who Pacifies the East, and Inspector of Eastern Yang Province — in all editions Eastern is lacking before Yang Province; Beishi vol. 29 has it.

sentences.zh: 按卷八世宗紀景明四年四月記蕭寶夤官也是「東揚州刺史」。

translations.literal: According to the Annals of Emperor Shizong in juan 8, the entry for the fourth month of Jingming year 4 records Xiao Baoyin's office likewise as "Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou."
translations.idiomatic: The Annals of Emperor Shizong in juan 8 likewise records Xiao Baoyin's office in the fourth month of Jingming year 4 as Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 寶夤都督三州，「東揚」居首，照例首列所督為哪一州，即是此州刺史，且當時揚州刺史是任城王澄。

translations.literal: Baoyin was Commander of three provinces; "Eastern Yang" stands first. By convention the first province listed is the one of which he was Inspector, and at that time Inspector of Yangzhou was Prince Cheng of Ren.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin commanded three provinces, with Eastern Yang listed first. By convention the lead province is the one he governed as inspector—and at the time Yangzhou was held by Prince Cheng of Ren.

sentences.zh: 知脫「東」字無疑，今據北史補。

translations.literal: Thus the omission of the character "Eastern" is beyond doubt; we now supplement according to the History of the North.
translations.idiomatic: The omission of "Eastern" is certain; the text is restored here from the History of the North.

sentences.zh: 亦知其若斯 諸本「若」作「苦」，獨局本作「若」。

translations.literal: Also knowing that it was so: in all editions ruo (if/so) is written as ku (bitter); only the Ju edition has ruo.
translations.idiomatic: Also knowing that it was so: all editions read ku (bitter) for ruo (if/so); only the Ju edition preserves ruo.

sentences.zh: 按作「苦」於文義不協，今從局本。

translations.literal: We consider that reading it as "bitter" does not accord with the sense; we now follow the Ju edition.
translations.idiomatic: Reading ku (bitter) does not fit the sense; we follow the Ju edition.

sentences.zh: 又破其金城王莫折普賢於水洛城 諸本「水」作「永」，冊府卷三五四

translations.literal: Again defeated Moqi Puxian, King of Jincheng, at Shuilo city: in all editions shui (water) is written as yong; Cefu yuangui juan 354
translations.idiomatic: Again defeated Moqi Puxian, King of Jincheng, at Shuilo city—all editions read yong for shui (water); Cefu yuangui juan 354

sentences.zh: 〈四二０一頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 4201〉

sentences.zh: 作「水」。

translations.literal: has shui (water).
translations.idiomatic: reads shui (water).

sentences.zh: 按水洛口、水洛亭，見水經注卷一七渭水篇。

translations.literal: We note that Shuilo Pass and Shuilo Pavilion appear in the Commentary on the Water Classic, juan 17, Wei River section.
translations.idiomatic: Shuilo Pass and Shuilo Pavilion appear in the Commentary on the Water Classic, juan 17, on the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 「永」字訛，今據改。

translations.literal: The character yong is erroneous; we now emend accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Yong is a scribal error and is emended here accordingly.
